sweeps.topic: Simulation platforms and procedures for training a companion quadruped's social + physical behavior (locomotion, expression, social decision, dialogue), with a layered sim design for Parcel's Go2

findings.claim: Habitat 3.0 simulates SMPL-X humanoid avatars (12 base models, AMASS walking clips played cyclically to waypoints) alongside a Spot robot, with a Social Navigation task (follow a walking human at 1-2 m) and a human-in-the-loop VR/keyboard tool; it does not simulate audio or speech.
findings.source_title: Habitat 3.0: A Co-Habitat for Humans, Avatars and Robots
findings.numbers: robot 245±19 FPS single env; humanoid 188±2 FPS; robot+humanoid 136±8 FPS single env, 1191±3 FPS across 16 envs on one GPU; social-nav RL: DD-PPO, 200M env steps ≈ 4 days on 4 A100, 24 envs/GPU; results heuristic expert S 1.00 / SPS 0.97 / F 0.51 / CR 0.52 vs end-to-end RL S 0.97 / SPS 0.65 / F 0.44 / CR 0.51; HITL 30 participants, RE 123%/134%; ZSC unseen-partner SR 71.7%; habitat-lab MIT
findings.relevance: Direct template for the 'look back at the owner when lost' decision layer: scripted walking owner, follow band, finding/following/collision metrics; also shows the learned social-nav policy barely beats a heuristic, so the scripted-follow + learned-when-to-look-back split is cheaper.

findings.claim: SoundSpaces 2.0 (habitat-sim audio sensor) is the only platform in this set that renders acoustics: bi-directional ray-traced RIRs with 7 mic layouts including binaural and ambisonics and custom mono arrays; it is CPU-bound and slow, and generates no speech itself.
findings.source_title: SoundSpaces 2.0: A Simulation Platform for Visual-Acoustic Learning
findings.numbers: high-quality 0.9 FPS (1 thread) / 4.0 FPS (5 threads); high-speed 7.7 / 33.5 FPS on Xeon Gold 6230; ASR WER 29.10% → 12.48% fine-tuned on sim IRs vs 13.32% on real IRs; continuous audio-nav success 64.7% vs 0.9% grid; 0.15 m steps
findings.relevance: Use offline to render TTS/recorded owner speech and laughter through room acoustics for the XVF3800 array (DoA, 'owner called from behind'); far too slow for the 50 Hz RL loop.

findings.claim: MetaUrban provides the largest open animated-human library among these platforms (1,100 rigged humans × 2,314 BEDLAM motions, 10,000 obstacles) with a Boston Dynamics Spot 'robot dog' agent, but it is a Panda3D kinematic urban simulator at ~60 FPS with no Go2, audio or speech.
findings.source_title: MetaUrban: An Embodied AI Simulation Platform for Urban Micromobility
findings.numbers: 10,000 obstacles; 1,100 rigged humans (68 garments, 32 hairs, 13 beards, 46 accessories, 1,038 textures); 2,314 movements (2,311 from BEDLAM); agents: delivery bot, wheelchair, scooter, Spot, humanoid; ~60 FPS, ~2 GB GPU; PPO PointNav SR 66% SPL 0.64 cost 0.51; PPO SocialNav SR 34% SNS 0.64 cost 0.66; code Apache-2.0, paper CC BY 4.0
findings.relevance: Source of human animation and crowd behaviour for a future 'walk beside the owner outdoors' layer; not a body-level trainer.

findings.claim: Isaac Lab ships Unitree Go2 velocity environments and a Go2 asset with a DC-motor actuator model, and publishes single-GPU throughput for velocity-tracking tasks; NVIDIA's Spot recipe trained 4096 envs for ~4 h on an RTX 4090 and transferred zero-shot with inference on a Jetson Orin.
findings.source_title: Isaac Lab Performance Benchmarks (+ environments list, unitree.py asset config, NVIDIA Spot blog)
findings.numbers: Isaac-Velocity-Flat/Rough-Unitree-Go2-v0; UNITREE_GO2_CFG DCMotorCfg effort_limit 23.5, saturation 23.5, velocity_limit 30, stiffness 25, damping 0.5 (BSD-3); RTX 4090, 4096 envs G1 rough: 94k env-steps/s sim-only, 88k w/ inference, 82k w/ training; L40 72k/64k/62k; 4×L40 290k; 6.5 GB RAM / 6.1 GB VRAM; Spot: 4096 envs, 15,000 iterations ≈ 4 h on RTX 4090, 85–95k FPS, MLP [512,256,128], zero-shot on hardware
findings.relevance: Reference locomotion trainer with the Go2 already modelled; the readiness verdict already picked Isaac Lab → MuJoCo as the cross-simulator check; throughput sets the budget for the L0 layer.

findings.claim: Unitree's official MuJoCo-based RL repo (unitree_rl_mjlab, on mjlab/MuJoCo Warp) supports Go2 with a Unitree-Go2-Flat velocity task and motion-imitation tasks, mirroring unitree_rl_lab (Isaac Lab 2.3.0 / Isaac Sim 5.1.0, Go2/H1/G1) and unitree_rl_gym (Isaac Gym, BSD-3); a community Go1 benchmark puts mjlab at 190k vs Isaac Lab 240k steps/s at 4096 envs.
findings.source_title: unitree_rl_mjlab (+ unitree_rl_lab, unitree_rl_gym, mjlab discussion #220, mujoco_warp)
findings.numbers: Go2, A2, As2, G1, R1, H1_2, H2 supported; tasks Unitree-Go2-Flat etc.; Apache-2.0; mjlab requires NVIDIA GPU, Apache-2.0; MuJoCo Warp lacks IMPLICITFAST, PGS/noslip, plugin actuators; Go1 flat 4096 envs: mjlab 190k steps/s (25% VRAM, ETA 1h30) vs Isaac Lab 240k; mis-installed mjlab 11k vs 72k at 1024 envs
findings.relevance: The MuJoCo-native path matching Parcel's mujoco 3.11 pin: replaces the refuted Go2Env with an official Go2 task without an Isaac Sim install, and is the exact stack Uni-Mo used for real-Go2 expressive transfer.

findings.claim: MuJoCo Playground (MJX) trains quadruped joystick policies in minutes on one or two consumer GPUs with published per-environment throughput and zero-shot Go1 transfer; Go2 is not among its environments but mujoco_menagerie ships a BSD-3 Go2 model with an MJX (sphere-collision) variant.
findings.source_title: MuJoCo Playground (+ mujoco_menagerie unitree_go2)
findings.numbers: A100 env-steps/s: Go1 Joystick Flat 417,451±2,955; Go1 Handstand 204,416; Go1 Footstand 204,578; Go1 Getup 96,173; Spot Joystick 404,931; Barkour 385,920; Go1 joystick trained within 5 min on 2×RTX 4090; Berkeley Humanoid <15 min; G1/T1 <30 min; pixels: Cartpole ~403k, Franka PickCube ~37k steps/s; Franka pixels 100% in 12 real trials; code Apache-2.0, paper CC BY 4.0; Go2 menagerie BSD-3 from unitree_ros URDF
findings.relevance: Establishes the 'minutes on one GPU' order of magnitude for a 12-DoF quadruped and the Go2 model to swap in; note mjx is not importable in Parcel's venv today.

findings.claim: Genesis is Apache-2.0, includes a Go2 locomotion training example (4096 envs, rsl_rl PPO) and claims 10–80× speedups over Isaac Gym/Sim/Lab and MJX, but no FPS figure or Go2 sim-to-real result appeared on any fetched page.
findings.source_title: Genesis go2_train.py (+ README, docs overview)
findings.numbers: --num-envs 4096 default; rsl-rl-lib>=5.0.0; --max-iterations 101; num_steps_per_env 24; episode_length_s 20; rewards tracking_lin_vel 1.0, tracking_ang_vel 0.2, lin_vel_z -1.0, base_height -50, action_rate -0.005, similar_to_default -0.1; docs: '10–80× faster than ... Isaac Gym/Sim/Lab and MuJoCo MJX'; license Apache 2.0
findings.relevance: Viable second choice for L0 with a tiny script; unverified speed claims and no maintainer Go2 sim-to-real make it lower priority than MuJoCo Warp/mjlab.

findings.claim: ProcTHOR procedurally generates 10,000 interactive houses from 16 scene specs and 1,633 interactable assets in AI2-THOR, runs at thousands of FPS with 15 processes on one GPU, and its pretraining improved ObjectNav/rearrangement SOTA; it has no people, audio or Go2 physics.
findings.source_title: ProcTHOR: Large-Scale Embodied AI Using Procedural Generation
findings.numbers: 10,000 train + 1,000 val + 1,000 test houses; 16 scene specifications; 1,633 interactable instances / 108 object types; 1,427±74 to 6,280±40 FPS (15 processes, one GPU); Habitat 2022 ObjectNav >3 SPL; RoboTHOR ObjectNav +8.8 SPL; Rearrangement 0.19→0.245; procthor repo Apache-2.0
findings.relevance: Cheapest source of thousands of distinct home layouts for a 'where did the owner go' curriculum, paired with Habitat/IRA humans.

findings.claim: Isaac Sim's people animation (omni.anim.people) is deprecated in favour of Isaacsim.Replicator.Agent, whose characters are scripted via GoTo/Idle/LookAround/Sit/Queue command files on a NavMesh and whose only supported robots are Nova Carter and iw.hub; nothing documents characters reacting to a robot.
findings.source_title: Isaac Sim 5.1.0 IRA Actor Control (+ ext_omni_anim_people deprecation notice, tutorial_replicator_agent)
findings.numbers: commands: GoTo x y z yaw, Idle seconds, LookAround seconds, Sit /World/Chair seconds, Queue; robots Nova Carter, iw.hub (GoTo/Idle/LiftUp/LiftDown); runtime command injection 'only works while the simulation is running'; 'IRA requires a NavMesh'
findings.relevance: Shows Isaac's humans are a synthetic-data tool, not a social partner: the owner's physical trajectory can be scripted this way, but reactions must come from an LLM agent layer.

findings.claim: SOTOPIA defines LLM-vs-LLM social role-play with a 7-dimension evaluator, and SOTOPIA-π shows a 7B model trained on self-play filtered by GPT-4 reaches GPT-4-level judge scores while the gap between GPT-4 ratings and human ratings widens.
findings.source_title: SOTOPIA-π: Interactive Learning of Socially Intelligent Language Agents (+ SOTOPIA)
findings.numbers: SOTOPIA: 90 scenarios, 40 characters, 5 relationship types, 450 tasks; 20 hard tasks; GPT-4 goal 4.85 vs human 5.95; 200 human-rated episodes, κ 0.503; SOTOPIA-π: Mistral-7B, 100 tasks/round, 10 interactions/task; goal on hard tasks GPT-4-rated 3.25→5.71 (GPT-4 5.89), human-rated 2.89→4.29 (GPT-4 5.25); MMLU 49.21→48.57; toxic words 0.9 vs 3.6; repo MIT
findings.relevance: The canonical recipe for training a social policy against LLM partners, and the canonical warning: judge-optimised social policies overstate progress unless a human-rated hold-out is kept — this drives the 'recorded owner calibration set' requirement.

findings.claim: τ-bench simulates the user with gpt-4-0613 from a task instruction and shows even gpt-4o is unreliable across trials; τ2-bench adds an MIT-licensed full-duplex voice user-simulation mode over realtime providers.
findings.source_title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction (+ tau2-bench repo)
findings.numbers: retail 115 tasks, airline 50; user = gpt-4-0613; pass^k = E[C(c,k)/C(n,k)]; gpt-4o pass^1 61.2 retail / 35.2 airline; pass^8 <25% retail; tau2 domains mock, airline, retail, telecom, banking_knowledge; 'End-to-end voice evaluation with realtime providers (OpenAI, Gemini, xAI)'; MIT
findings.relevance: Closest existing harness for a full-duplex voice owner simulator and for measuring consistency (pass^k) of the dog's dialogue policy within the Realtime API budget.

findings.claim: Purpose-built User LMs simulate humans better than prompted assistant models ('better assistants yield worse simulators'), and simulators fine-tuned on real human utterances produce assistants that win against real users far more than role-play-prompted simulators; surveys list over-cooperativeness and persona drift as systematic LLM-user failure modes.
findings.source_title: Quantifying the Utility of User Simulators for Building Collaborative LLM Assistants (+ Flipping the Dialogue, user-simulation survey)
findings.numbers: assistants trained against fine-tuned simulators: 58% win over initial, 57% over role-play-trained; User LMs: GPT-4o eval 74.6% → 57.4% when judged against User LMs; survey failure modes: persona 'drift in style, beliefs, or goals', 'unrealistically cooperative', 'overly polite, homogeneous behavior'
findings.relevance: Decides where the owner must be recorded rather than LLM-simulated: seed and fine-tune the owner sim on real transcripts and validate on real-owner sessions, or the learned social behaviour will not transfer.

findings.claim: A PRISMA review of 86 LLM-in-HRI studies finds humanoids (Pepper, Nao, Furhat) dominate and surfaces no study that trains a robot policy against LLM-simulated humans; LLM social simulations are judged usable only for pilot/exploratory studies.
findings.source_title: How Do We Research Human-Robot Interaction in the Age of Large Language Models? A Systematic Review (+ 'LLM Social Simulations Are a Promising Research Method')
findings.numbers: 86 studies reviewed; only ChatGPT-generated feedback data (ChatAdp) as synthetic human input; 'can already be used for pilot and exploratory studies'
findings.relevance: 'Sims for HRI' is an open gap: Parcel's LLM-owner RL loop would be early, so it must ship with human-rated validation rather than lean on precedent.

findings.claim: HumanML3D pairs 14,616 SMPL motions with 44,970 texts and is the standard text-to-motion base; Habitat 3.0 documents driving avatars with off-the-shelf text-to-motion models, and MDME shows AMASS human motion plus only ~10 min of dog motion (augmented to 52 min) suffices to embed styles for a 50 Hz quadruped/humanoid tracking policy in Isaac Lab.
findings.source_title: HumanML3D (+ Habitat 3.0 project page, Multi-Domain Motion Embedding)
findings.numbers: 14,616 motions, 44,970 descriptions, 5,371 words, 28.59 h, 20 fps, 2–10 s clips (mean 7.1 s), 22-joint SMPL, repo MIT; MDME: AMASS + ~10 min dog data → 52 min augmented, PPO in Isaac Lab, 50 Hz, 30k/40k iterations, ANYmal D + Fourier N1 hardware
findings.relevance: Unlimited owner gestures for the avatar side via text-to-motion; quadruped motion data is scarce, which motivates generated references (Uni-Mo) for the dog's expression library.

findings.claim: Eureka (GPT-4 reward code, Isaac Gym) beats human-engineered rewards on most tasks, and Eurekaverse (GPT-4o terrain curricula) trained a Go1 parkour policy that transferred to real obstacles for ~$15 of API and one day on 8 GPUs.
findings.source_title: Eurekaverse: Environment Curriculum Generation via Large Language Models (+ Eureka)
findings.numbers: Eureka: 29 envs, 10 morphologies, beats humans on 83%, +52% normalised, 16 samples × 5 iterations, gpt-4-0314, Isaac Gym Preview 4, MIT; Eurekaverse: GPT-4o, Go1 12 DoF, 5 generations × 8 parallel runs × 2000 steps, ~24 h on 8×A6000 48 GB, ~$15 API, real jumps to 75 cm, climbs >50 cm, 30° ramp, 10 trials/difficulty, MIT
findings.relevance: Proven for LLM-written physical rewards and terrain curricula; for the social layer, LLM-written rewards inherit the judge-gap problem and should be proposals a human approves.

findings.claim: Uni-Mo turns language prompts into 7,488 quadruped motion clips via a fine-tuned video diffusion model and URDF-anchored 4D lifting, trains PPO tracking policies in MuJoCo (MjLab, BeyondMimic setup), and deploys 392 random motions on a real Go2 with 96.7% success — expressive, non-locomotion motion on Go2 is a solved tracking problem once a reference exists.
findings.source_title: Unleashing Infinite Motion: Scaling Expressive Quadrupedal Motion via Generative Video Priors (Uni-Mo)
findings.numbers: Quad-Imaginarium 7,488 clips at 24 fps, 18.5 h; Wan2.2-I2V-A14B + LoRA fine-tuned on 56 H20 GPUs; ViTPose fine-tuned on renders + URDF-anchored optimisation; PPO tracking on one RTX 3090 per motion; sim success 97.6%; real Go2 392 motions × 5 trials = 96.7%; CC BY 4.0
findings.relevance: Shows the exact stack (MuJoCo + mjlab tracking) and the bottleneck (reference library, not the controller) for Parcel's chuckle/bow/stretch/look-back vocabulary; the sole source for this scale of Go2 expressive transfer.

findings.claim: Spatio-Temporal Motion Retargeting transfers dog mocap and animator-authored clips to Go1/Go2/AlienGo/B2 with an Isaac Gym-trained tracking policy at 48.7 mm keypoint error after one GPU-hour, and the canonical Peng 2020 / AMP 2021 works establish animal-imitation and discriminator style rewards as the standard expression recipe.
findings.source_title: Spatio-Temporal Motion Retargeting for Quadruped Robots (+ Peng et al. 2020, AMP 2021)
findings.numbers: six motions (Trot0/1, Pace0/1, SideSteps, HopTurn); mean keypoint error 48.7 mm vs 88.4–275.3 mm baselines; ~50M samples ≈ 1 h on RTX A6000; deployed on Go1, Go2, AlienGo, B2; Peng 2020: 18-DoF quadruped, animal reference + domain adaptation; AMP: style reward from unstructured clips, separate task reward
findings.relevance: Gives the per-clip training cost (~1 GPU-hour) and the AMP regulariser so composed expressions stay dog-like on the Go2.

findings.claim: The open Spot RL sim-to-real pipeline (Isaac Lab + RSL_RL, sim parameters tuned by Wasserstein/MMD + CMA-ES against hardware data) reached 5.2 m/s vs the 1.6 m/s default controller; Boston Dynamics' own expressive motion (Choreographer) remains authored and requires a special-permissions licence; Sony's aibo home dog was trained with sim-to-real RL to walk quietly, beating hand-tuned commercial controllers.
findings.source_title: High-Performance Reinforcement Learning on Spot (+ Spot Choreography SDK docs, Learning Quiet Walking for a Small Home Robot)
findings.numbers: Spot: 5.2 m/s flying trot vs 1.6 m/s default; code via Isaac Lab and Boston Dynamics; Choreography 'requires a special-permissions license'; aibo ICRA 2025: RL foot-contact-velocity minimisation with learned per-joint PD gains, quieter than 'carefully handcrafted Sony commercial controllers'
findings.relevance: Vendor expressive motion is scripted (the baseline Parcel is trying to move past), sim-parameter identification from hardware data is the proven bridge, and quietness is a home-companion objective worth adding to L0.

design_implications: No single simulator covers body + people + speech: train each layer where its throughput lives (physics ~100k-400k steps/s for L0/L1, kinematic humanoid sim ~100-1000 FPS for L2, LLM-bound for L3) and connect layers through the existing contracts (skills, body-intent lane, reaction arbiter, safety).

L0/L1 should run on MuJoCo Warp via mjlab / unitree_rl_mjlab (Unitree-Go2-Flat, Apache-2.0) with the BSD-3 Menagerie Go2 model: it matches Parcel's mujoco 3.11 pin, avoids an Isaac Sim install in the 12-hour window, replaces the refuted Go2Env by construction, and is the same stack Uni-Mo used for 96.7% real-Go2 expressive transfer; keep Isaac Lab Isaac-Velocity-Rough-Unitree-Go2-v0 only as the cross-simulator transfer check.

The trainable object for expression is a single motion-tracking policy over a parameterised reference library (chuckle, bow, stretch, look-back, nod) with an AMP style discriminator; references are authored keyframes or generated (video-prior pipeline), and cost ~1 GPU-hour per clip set. This replaces the fixed command list with skills that take intensity/duration/gaze parameters.

'Look back when lost' trains in a Habitat 3.0-style follow task (scripted owner waypoints, 1-2 m band, S/F/CR metrics) at the decision level; the learned part is when to fire the look-back skill on detection loss, since Habitat's learned social-nav policy (S 0.97, F 0.44) does not beat its heuristic expert (S 1.00, F 0.51).

'Chuckle if the joke was funny' trains in an abstract social sim with an LLM owner agent that emits utterances, a latent funniness and a laugh/no-laugh reaction; the policy learns chuckle intensity and timing (during vs after the punchline — the full-duplex decision at 5-10 Hz, executed at 50 Hz by L1/L0).

Owner simulation split: LLM agent for dialogue content, affect trajectory and reactions; scripted for physical trajectories, timing and safety-critical positions (Habitat/IRA GoTo-style); recorded for voice, prosody, laughter and — critically — a human-rated calibration/hold-out set, because judge-optimised social policies inflate LLM-judge scores more than human scores (SOTOPIA-π 5.71 vs 4.29) and fine-tuned-on-real-human simulators transfer better (58%/57% win rates).

Audio is never simulated as speech by any platform; use SoundSpaces 2.0 offline (custom 4-mono-mic array matching the XVF3800) to render TTS/recorded owner audio through room acoustics for DoA detectors, not inside RL loops (0.9-33.5 FPS).

Budget fit: run the LLM owner and judge locally for training-scale episodes (text budget <= $100/mo), and reserve the Realtime API (<= $300/mo) for tau2-bench-style full-duplex voice evaluation episodes only.
LLM-written rewards/curricula (Eureka/Eurekaverse) are proven for the physical layers and should be used there; for the social layer treat LLM-written rewards as human-approved proposals.

The deterministic safety layer stays above every learned layer: all sources that transferred expressive motion tracked references under a low-level controller, and quietness (aibo) plus fall recovery (Playground getup) belong in L0 objectives for a home companion.

trainable_options.name: Go2 velocity + getup policy on MuJoCo Warp (unitree_rl_mjlab / mjlab)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Isaac-Lab-style manager-based PPO (rsl_rl) velocity-tracking and recovery policies for the Go2 on GPU MuJoCo, with Unitree's sim2sim (unitree_mujoco) and sim2real (unitree_sdk2) path
trainable_options.license: Apache-2.0 (mjlab Apache-2.0; Menagerie Go2 BSD-3)
trainable_options.inputs: proprioception (joint pos/vel, base ang vel, projected gravity), previous action, velocity command
trainable_options.outputs: 12 joint position targets at 50 Hz
trainable_options.train_recipe: 4096 envs, PPO, domain randomisation of mass/friction/motor strength/pushes; Go1-class throughput 190k steps/s at 4096 envs; expect tens of minutes to ~1.5 h per policy on one GPU
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: High: NVIDIA's Spot policy ran inference on a Jetson Orin; a small MLP at 50 Hz is trivial for the AGX Orin 64 GB

trainable_options.name: Expression motion-tracking policy (Uni-Mo / STMR / BeyondMimic recipe)
trainable_options.what_it_is: A single PPO tracking policy that reproduces a library of kinematic reference clips (chuckle, bow, stretch, look-back, nod) on the Go2, optionally with an AMP discriminator for dog-like style
trainable_options.license: Paper CC BY 4.0; Uni-Mo dataset release stated but licence not verified; STMR code availability not stated
trainable_options.size_params: MLP tracking policy conditioned on reference phase/keypoints (per-motion or multi-motion)
trainable_options.inputs: proprioception + reference trajectory features (target joint angles / keypoints, phase)
trainable_options.outputs: 12 joint position targets at 50 Hz
trainable_options.train_recipe: references from authored keyframes, retargeted dog mocap, or generated video priors; PPO in MuJoCo/mjlab, ~50M samples ≈ 1 GPU-hour per clip set (STMR, A6000); one RTX 3090 per motion (Uni-Mo); real Go2 96.7% over 392 motions
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: High for the tracking policy; the reference-generation pipeline (Wan2.2 video model, ViTPose lifting) stays offline on the desktop

trainable_options.name: Social decision / body-intent policy trained against an LLM owner (SOTOPIA-π-style self-play + Habitat 3.0 follow task)
trainable_options.what_it_is: A small policy (or fine-tuned small LM) mapping state-of-world features (owner visibility/pose, utterance affect, joke events, owner-model facts, timers) to expression-skill selection, intensity and timing; trained by filtered behaviour cloning + self-reinforcement against an LLM owner agent with scripted trajectories, judged by an LLM evaluator calibrated on human ratings
trainable_options.license: sotopia repo MIT; habitat-lab MIT
trainable_options.size_params: Mistral-7B in SOTOPIA-π; for Parcel a 0.5-3B local LM or an MLP/GRU over a feature vector
trainable_options.inputs: discrete-continuous world-state features at 5-10 Hz, dialogue state from L3
trainable_options.outputs: skill id + parameters (intensity, duration, gaze target) into the 50 Hz body-intent lane
trainable_options.train_recipe: 100 tasks/round × 10 interactions (SOTOPIA-π); Habitat social-nav: 200M steps on 4 A100 for end-to-end RL (avoid — learn only the look-back trigger on top of a scripted follower); keep a 30-50 episode human-rated hold-out because GPT-4-rated 5.71 vs human 4.29
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: High for an MLP/GRU; medium for a 1-3B LM at 5-10 Hz alongside the voice stack on the Orin

trainable_options.name: Owner user-simulator (User LM fine-tuned on recorded owner sessions; tau2-bench voice mode for eval)
trainable_options.what_it_is: A purpose-built user LM (persona + memory + affect) that stands in for the owner during L2/L3 training, fine-tuned on consented owner transcripts; tau2-bench's realtime-provider voice mode used only for full-duplex evaluation episodes
trainable_options.license: tau2-bench MIT; UserLM papers CC (weights per their releases, not verified here)
trainable_options.size_params: UserLM-8b class in the literature; Parcel can use a 7-8B local model
trainable_options.inputs: dialogue history, scenario/persona spec, scripted physical-event timeline
trainable_options.outputs: owner utterances, affect/laugh events, occasional non-cooperative or distracted behaviour
trainable_options.train_recipe: fine-tune on real human utterances rather than role-play prompting (58%/57% downstream win rates); avoid using the assistant model as the simulator ('better assistants yield worse simulators')
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: Not deployed on the robot; runs on the desktop during training

trainable_options.name: LLM-generated rewards and terrain curricula (Eureka / Eurekaverse) for L0
trainable_options.what_it_is: GPT-4-class code generation of reward functions and progressively harder terrains, evolved by training feedback
trainable_options.license: MIT (both repos)
trainable_options.size_params: n/a (uses hosted GPT-4o; ~$15 API per Eurekaverse run)
trainable_options.inputs: environment source code + training statistics
trainable_options.outputs: reward code / terrain generation code
trainable_options.train_recipe: Eureka: 16 samples × 5 iterations; Eurekaverse: 5 generations × 8 parallel runs × 2000 steps, ~24 h on 8×A6000 (Isaac Gym); would need porting to MuJoCo/mjlab
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: n/a (offline tooling)

open_questions: Go2-specific env-steps/s on MuJoCo Warp vs Isaac Lab on the RTX 5000 Ada is unmeasured; the closest evidence is Go1 (mjlab 190k vs Isaac Lab 240k at 4096 envs) and A100 MJX Go1 417k. Does mujoco_warp install cleanly against Parcel's venv (mjx is not importable today)?

No fetched source trains a robot's social policy against LLM-simulated humans and validates it with real humans; the 86-study HRI review found none. How large must Parcel's recorded-owner calibration set be for the LLM-judge gap to be bounded?

Uni-Mo's Quad-Imaginarium dataset licence, download, and motion categories (does it contain 'laugh'/'chuckle'-like clips?) were not readable; verify before adopting it as the expression reference library.
Genesis's headline FPS claims were absent from every fetched page; treat '10-80×' as unverified until benchmarked locally.
The DFM dance-motion paper and SOTOPIA-RL could not be fetched (search budget exhausted); they may add evidence for music-timed expression and social-reward design.

How should 'funniness' ground truth be produced in sim: LLM owner's self-reported laugh, an independent judge, or replayed recorded laughter from the owner? The literature's over-cooperative-user bias suggests the LLM owner will laugh too often.
Full-duplex timing: what is the acceptable latency from punchline detection to chuckle onset, and can the 5-10 Hz L2 decision plus 50 Hz L1 execution meet it on the Orin alongside the voice stack?

results.claim: Habitat 3.0 simulates SMPL-X humanoid avatars (12 base models, AMASS walking clips played cyclically to waypoints) alongside a Spot robot, with a Social Navigation task (follow a walking human at 1-2 m) and a human-in-the-loop VR/keyboard tool; it does not simulate audio or speech.
results.evidence_quote: "we cache 4 male, 4 female and 4 neutral body shapes" ... "a walking motion clip from the AMASS dataset...trim it to contain a single walking cycle...play it cyclically" ... "a humanoid walks in a scene, and the robot must locate and follow the humanoid while maintaining a safety distance ranging from 1m to 2m" ... "humans can collaborate with an autonomous robot using mouse and keyboard inputs or a virtual reality (VR) interface" ... "a robot operates at 245±19 frames per second (FPS)"; "the humanoid achieves 188±2 FPS"; "robot-humanoid achieves 136±8"; 16 envs: "robot-humanoid reaching 1191±3 FPS" ... "DD-PPO...distributing training across 4 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Each GPU runs 24 parallel environments...about 200 million environment steps (roughly 4 days of training)" ... "Both Plan-Pop3 and Learn-Single improve RE to 123% and 134% respectively" ... "the highest ZSC-pop-eval SR of 71.7%"
results.correction: All numbers check out against the HTML full text: heuristic expert S 1.00 / SPS 0.97 / F 0.51 / CR 0.52 vs end-to-end RL S 0.97 / SPS 0.65 / F 0.44 / CR 0.51; 30 HITL participants. The paper contains no mention of audio, speech, or sound, so 'does not simulate audio or speech' is supported by absence. habitat-lab's GitHub README states 'Habitat-Lab is MIT licensed' (the arXiv page itself only shows the arXiv non-exclusive license).

results.claim: Isaac Lab ships Unitree Go2 velocity environments and a Go2 asset with a DC-motor actuator model, and publishes single-GPU throughput for velocity-tracking tasks; NVIDIA's Spot recipe trained 4096 envs for ~4 h on an RTX 4090 and transferred zero-shot with inference on a Jetson Orin.
results.evidence_quote: Isaac-Velocity-Rough-G1-v0, 4096 envs, RTX 4090: "Environment Step FPS" is "94000", "Environment Step and Inference FPS" is "88000", "Environment Step, Inference, and Train FPS" is "82000"; L40: 72000 / 64000 / 62000; 4x L40: 290000 / 270000 / 250000; "RAM (GB)" 6.5, "VRAM (GB)" 6.1. Environments page: "Isaac-Velocity-Flat-Unitree-Go2-v0", "Isaac-Velocity-Rough-Unitree-Go2-v0". unitree.py: DCMotorCfg "effort_limit=23.5", "saturation_effort=23.5", "velocity_limit=30.0", "stiffness=25.0", "damping=0.5", "SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause". NVIDIA blog: "With 4,096 environments and 15,000 iterations, equivalent to approximately 4 hours of training time on the NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU"; "achieved a training speed of 85,000 to 95,000 frames per second (FPS)"; "Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) with three layers, containing [512, 256, 128] neurons"; "deploying the policy trained in simulation to the real Spot robot on Jetson Orin zero shot"
results.correction: No correction needed. Note the performance-benchmark page itself benchmarks the G1 velocity task (not Go2); the Go2 environment IDs come from the environments list page and the Go2 actuator numbers from source/isaaclab_assets/isaaclab_assets/robots/unitree.py, exactly as the claim's title indicates.

results.claim: Unitree's official MuJoCo-based RL repo (unitree_rl_mjlab, on mjlab/MuJoCo Warp) supports Go2 with a Unitree-Go2-Flat velocity task and motion-imitation tasks, mirroring unitree_rl_lab (Isaac Lab 2.3.0 / Isaac Sim 5.1.0, Go2/H1/G1) and unitree_rl_gym (Isaac Gym, BSD-3); a community Go1 benchmark puts mjlab at 190k vs Isaac Lab 240k steps/s at 4096 envs.
results.evidence_quote: unitree_rl_mjlab: "currently supporting Unitree Go2, A2, As2, G1, R1, H1_2 and H2"; "a reinforcement learning project built upon the mjlab, using MuJoCo as its physics simulation backend"; tasks Unitree-Go2-Flat, Unitree-G1-Tracking-No-State-Estimation; Apache-2.0. mjlab README: "mjlab requires an NVIDIA GPU for training"; Apache-2.0; "mjlab combines Isaac Lab's manager-based API with MuJoCo Warp". mujoco_warp README: "IMPLICITFAST midpoint integrator feature is not supported"; "PGS and noslip not yet supported"; "PLUGIN types not yet supported". mjlab discussion #220 (alaurenzi, Go1): 1024 envs "11k steps/s" mjlab vs "72k steps/s" Isaac Lab; 4096 envs "190k steps/s" mjlab "25% VRAM usage" "ETA 1h 30min" vs "240k steps/s" Isaac Lab. unitree_rl_lab badges: Isaac Lab "2.3.0", Isaac Sim "5.1.0", robots "Go2, H1, G1-29dof". unitree_rl_gym: "Isaac Gym" and "Mujoco", "BSD-3-Clause License".
results.correction: No numeric correction needed. Minor nuances: the '11k vs 72k' mjlab figure was attributed in the thread to a mis-installation, as the claim says; unitree_rl_gym lists MuJoCo alongside Isaac Gym (for sim2sim), and unitree_rl_lab's G1 is the 29-DoF variant.

results.claim: MuJoCo Playground (MJX) trains quadruped joystick policies in minutes on one or two consumer GPUs with published per-environment throughput and zero-shot Go1 transfer; Go2 is not among its environments but mujoco_menagerie ships a BSD-3 Go2 model with an MJX (sphere-collision) variant.
results.evidence_quote: Abstract: "researchers can train policies in minutes on a single GPU" ... "zero-shot sim-to-real transfer". Body: "train the policy in flat ground with restricted command ranges within 5 minutes (2x RTX 4090)"; "Training on flat ground lasts under 15 minutes for the Berkeley Humanoid"; "under 30 minutes for the Unitree G1 and the Booster T1 on two RTX 4090". Table VII (A100 steps/s): Go1JoystickFlatTerrain "417451 ± 2955", Go1Handstand "204416 ± 738", Go1Footstand "204578 ± 906", Go1Getup "96173 ± 230", SpotFlatTerrainJoystick "404931 ± 2710", BarkourJoystick "385920 ± 2162". Fig. 6: CartpoleBalance "roughly 403,000 steps per second", PandaPickCubeCartesian "roughly 37,000". "Our policy achieves a 100% success rate in 12 real-world trials". "All four policies (joystick, handstand, footstand, and fall recovery) transfer robustly from simulation to reality". Table V lists Unitree Go1, G1, H1 — no Go2. "License: CC BY 4.0". Repo: "All other content in this repository is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0." Menagerie unitree_go2: BSD-3-Clause, from unitree_ros URDF, scene_mjx.xml replaces collision geometry with spheres since "MJX cannot deal with collision geoms other than spheres".
results.correction: No correction needed. All throughput and timing numbers match the HTML full text; the Go2 model facts come from the mujoco_menagerie unitree_go2 README as the claim's title indicates.

results.claim: SOTOPIA defines LLM-vs-LLM social role-play with a 7-dimension evaluator, and SOTOPIA-π shows a 7B model trained on self-play filtered by GPT-4 reaches GPT-4-level judge scores while the gap between GPT-4 ratings and human ratings widens.
results.evidence_quote: SOTOPIA-π: "The gap between GPT-4 scores and human scores increases as our method optimizes GPT-4 rated goal completion scores during training." Table (Automatic Evaluation on Hard Social Tasks, 28 data points): GPT-4 GOAL 5.89, Mistral-7B 3.25, BC+SR 5.71; (Human Evaluation, 28 data points): GPT-4 5.25, Mistral-7B 2.89, BC+SR 4.29; but (Automatic Evaluation on Hard Social Tasks, 140 data points): Mistral-7B 3.84. "Zhou et al. (2024) identified 14 hard social tasks SOTOPIA-hard among the original 90 social tasks" / "we select 14 hard social scenarios among 90 social scenarios". MMLU: Base 49.21, BC+SR 48.57; # Toxic: Base 3.6, BC+SR 0.9. SOTOPIA paper: "40 agents, 90 relationships, and 90 scenarios ... resulting in a set of 450 tasks"; "five types of relationships"; "seven dimensions"; "We use SOTOPIA-hard to refer to these 20 challenging tasks"; GPT-4 (w H) 4.85 vs Human (w G) 5.95*; "Randolph κ score of 0.503"; "We sampled 222 episodes (180 model-model episodes, and 42 episodes involving humans". sotopia-pi README: "Code License: Apache_2.0"; sotopia repo: MIT.
results.correction: The gist and headline numbers hold, but four details in the numbers field are off: (1) SOTOPIA human-rated episodes are 222 (180 model-model + 42 involving humans), not 200; (2) the SOTOPIA-π repository is Apache-2.0 — MIT is the license of the base sotopia repo; (3) SOTOPIA-hard is 20 tasks in the SOTOPIA paper, but SOTOPIA-π evaluates on a budget-limited subset of 14 of them; (4) the 3.25→5.71 GPT-4-rated hard-task figure is from the 28-data-point table aligned with the human evaluation — the 140-data-point automatic table gives Mistral-7B 3.84. Also, 5.71 vs 5.89 is 'near GPT-4-level' rather than reaching it.

results.claim: Purpose-built User LMs simulate humans better than prompted assistant models ('better assistants yield worse simulators'), and simulators fine-tuned on real human utterances produce assistants that win against real users far more than role-play-prompted simulators; surveys list over-cooperativeness and persona drift as systematic LLM-user failure modes.
results.evidence_quote: arXiv 2605.09808 abstract: "we measure pairwise win rates in a user study with 283 participants and on WildBench, a benchmark derived from real human–AI conversations"; "Training against the role-playing LLM yields an assistant statistically indistinguishable from the initial assistant in our user study (51% win rate)"; "training against the fine-tuned simulator yields significant gains (58% over the initial and 57% over the one trained against role-playing)"; "assistants trained against role-playing simulators fail to generalize when paired with other simulators at test time, while the one trained against fine-tuned simulator does." Flipping the Dialogue (arXiv 2510.06552, Naous et al.): "better assistants yield worse simulators"; GPT-4o performance drops from 74.6% to 57.4% when evaluated against User LMs in coding and math conversations. A Survey on LLM-based Conversational User Simulation (arXiv 2604.24977, Ni et al.): "often leading to drift in style, beliefs, or goals"; "Simulated users are also unrealistically cooperative"; "yielding overly polite, homogeneous behavior".
results.correction: All three sources support the claim as written. One calibration: 'far more' corresponds to 58% (fine-tuned simulator, statistically significant) versus 51% (role-play, indistinguishable from the initial assistant) in the 283-participant user study; the fine-tuned simulators were trained on WildChat human utterances.

sweeps.topic: Representing the "state of the world" (sensors, voice, user history, world state) as a learnable input for a full-duplex companion behavior model: world-model RL agents, multimodal state tokenization for embodied agents, long-term memory for companion agents, event/timestep encoding for continuous streams, personalization benchmarks, and a token-schema recommendation for a ~2-10 Hz state stream

findings.claim: DreamerV3 is a single-configuration world-model RL algorithm that outperforms specialized methods across 150+ tasks in 8 domains, with model sizes 12M-400M params, each agent trained on a single A100, and MIT-licensed code; larger models need less interaction to solve a task.
findings.source_title: Mastering diverse control tasks through world models (DreamerV3), Nature 640:647-653; arXiv 2301.04104; code github.com/danijar/dreamerv3
findings.numbers: 150+ tasks, 8 domains (Atari 57, ProcGen 16, DMLab 30, ...); 6 sizes 12M-400M params; single A100 per agent; diamonds in Minecraft within 100M env steps; symlog, two-hot returns, free bits clipped at 1 nat; MIT license (JAX reimplementation).
findings.relevance: The most credible off-the-shelf route to learn body-lane behavior from a vector/latent state (proprio + nav + owner channels) in MuJoCo on the Parcel desktop; does not read text/user history natively.

findings.claim: TD-MPC2 is a decoder-free latent world model + MPPI planner that trains 104 continuous-control tasks with one hyperparameter set and a 317M multitask model on 80 tasks; multi-embodiment handled by zero-padding, action masking, and a 96-D learnable task embedding; MIT code with 1M-317M checkpoints and a 545M-transition dataset.
findings.source_title: TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control (ICLR 2024); site tdmpc2.com; code github.com/nicklashansen/tdmpc2
findings.numbers: 104 online tasks in 4 domains; 80-task 317M model; sizes 1M/5M/19M/48M/317M; latent 512 (5M) to 1376 (317M); MPPI horizon 3; 5 Q-functions; proprio up to 223-D (Dog); pixels 64x64; datasets 545M transitions/2.69M episodes/34 GB and 345M/690k/20 GB; 324 checkpoints; single-task needs ~8 GB GPU, 317M multitask needs 24 GB GPU + 128 GB RAM; MIT.
findings.relevance: 5M model trains on the desktop and runs on Orin; the pad+mask+task-embedding trick is reusable for a state vector with optional channels (owner visible or not, speech on/off).

findings.claim: IRIS learns a token world model (16 discrete tokens per 64x64 frame, vocab 512, plus one action token per step) and reaches mean human-normalized 1.046 on Atari 100k after two hours of gameplay.
findings.source_title: Transformers are Sample-Efficient World Models (IRIS), ICLR 2023; code github.com/eloialonso/iris
findings.numbers: K=16 tokens/frame, N=512 vocab; transformer D=256, 10 layers, 4 heads, context L=20 steps; mean HNS 1.046, median 0.289, IQM 0.501; beats humans on 10/26 games; ~7 days on 8xA100-40GB for 2 envs per GPU (~3.5 GPU-days/game); GPL-3.0.
findings.relevance: Canonical proof that an observation-tokens-then-action-token sequence is a learnable world model at tiny scale; ancestor of the per-tick frame layout recommended for Parcel.

findings.claim: Delta-IRIS encodes each timestep as 4 delta tokens (40 bits) instead of IRIS's 16-64 tokens, is 25M params, trains ~10x faster (20 vs 2 FPS collection), and beats DreamerV3 XL (200M) on Crafter beyond 3M frames.
findings.source_title: Efficient World Models with Context-Aware Tokenization (Delta-IRIS), ICML 2024; code github.com/vmicheli/delta-iris
findings.numbers: 4 tokens/frame (4 x log2 1024 = 40 bits) vs IRIS 160 bits; 64x64 frames; 25M params vs IRIS 48M vs DreamerV3 XL 200M; Crafter 7.7 at 1M frames (IRIS 5.5), 16.1 at 10M frames solving 17/22 tasks; 20 FPS vs 2 FPS; sequence interleaves I-tokens, action tokens, delta-tokens; GPL-3.0; Crafter 5M checkpoint on HF.
findings.relevance: Justifies a ~4-token visual channel per 200 ms tick: tokenize deltas conditioned on a continuous context embedding rather than full frames.

findings.claim: Genie 3 generates navigable worlds at 24 fps / 720p with several minutes of consistency and ~1 minute of visual memory, but has a restricted action repertoire, multi-agent limits, and is only a limited research preview with no weights.
findings.source_title: Genie 3: A new frontier for world models (Google DeepMind blog)
findings.numbers: 24 fps; 720p; consistency 'several minutes'; memory 'as far back as one minute ago'; input response 'multiple times per second'; SIMA agent tested inside; limited research preview (5 Aug 2025).
findings.relevance: Not trainable or downloadable; irrelevant as a Parcel component, only evidence that generated worlds can host agent training loops.

findings.claim: 1X's learned world model evaluates policies: with 70% world-model accuracy and a 15% real success gap it picks the better policy 90% of the time; the public 1xgpt dataset is 100+ hours of 2 Hz, 16-frame, 16x16-token windows with raw actions (Apache 2.0); the 14B 1XWM policy needs ~13 s per 5 s of decision and scores 0-80% across tasks.
findings.source_title: 1X World Model (vendor pages: redwood-ai-world-model, 1x-world-model, world-model-self-learning; repo github.com/1x-technologies/1xgpt; challenge report arXiv 2510.07092)
findings.numbers: 70% WM accuracy + 15% gap -> 90% correct ranking (single-source, PDF did not parse); 3 tasks evaluated; dataset 100+ h, 16 images at 2 Hz per example, MAGVIT2 16x16 tokens for 256x256, factorized 2x2^9 vocab; GENIE_138M 8.79 CE at 0.075 s/frame, GENIE_35M 8.99 CE at 0.030 s/frame; 1XWM: 14B backbone, 900 h human video + 70 h NEO + 400 h IDM data, ~11 s + 1 s inference, 30 trials/task, 80% grab chips, 0% pour cereal; 8 parallel samples 30%->45%; challenge winners 23.0 dB PSNR, 6.6386 CE.
findings.relevance: Shows a modest-accuracy learned world model is useful for ranking policies before hardware; the 2 Hz tokenized-window format is an existence proof of a low-rate discrete state stream; the policy is far from duplex real time.

findings.claim: NVIDIA Cosmos provides open-weight video world foundation models (diffusion 7B/14B, autoregressive 4B/12B) and video tokenizers (4x8x8, 8x8x8, 8x16x16), trained on ~20M hours of video with 10,000 H100s for three months, with explicit post-training support for action-conditioned Video2World; models under NVIDIA Open Model License, code Apache 2.0.
findings.source_title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI; code github.com/nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-predict1
findings.numbers: ~20M h raw video; ~1e8 clips pretrain, ~1e7 finetune; 10,000 H100 x 3 months; diffusion 7B/14B, AR 4B/12B (5B/13B Video2World); tokenizers CV/DV 4x8x8, 8x8x8, 8x16x16 at 720p/360p; V-JEPA 2 reports a Cosmos-based planner at 4 min per action.
findings.relevance: Offline data/sim asset only (tokenizers, synthetic video); not an on-Orin component.

findings.claim: GAIA-2 is an 8.4B latent-diffusion world model conditioned on a structured state (ego speed/curvature, 3D agent boxes, weather, time of day, road semantics, country) generating up to 5 consistent camera views at 448x960; no weights/code release stated.
findings.source_title: GAIA-2: A Controllable Multi-View Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving (Wayve)
findings.numbers: tokenizer 85M encoder / 200M decoder; world model 8.4B; up to 5 cameras; 448x960; ~25M 2-second sequences; 20/25/30 Hz.
findings.relevance: Cleanest example of a world model driven by a structured ego+agents+environment state vector, which maps onto Parcel's robot-dynamics + owner/person list + room context.

findings.claim: V-JEPA 2 (1M+ hours video, up to 1B params, MIT code) provides strong frozen visual features; V-JEPA 2-AC (300M predictor, <62 h DROID data) plans zero-shot pick-and-place at 80% but needs 16 s per action.
findings.source_title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning; code github.com/facebookresearch/vjepa2
findings.numbers: 22M videos / 1M+ hours; checkpoints ViT-L 300M, ViT-H 600M, ViT-g 1B (2.1: ViT-B 80M, ViT-G 2B); AC predictor 300M, 24 layers, 16 heads, 1024 hidden; 7-D proprio; CEM planning; 16 s/action vs 4 min Cosmos baseline; Franka: reach 100%, grasp 70%/30%, pick-place 80%/80%; SSv2 77.3, EK100 R@5 39.7, PerceptionTest 84.0; MIT (+Apache-2.0 files).
findings.relevance: Use the ViT-B/L encoder frozen as the 1-4 pooled visual tokens per tick; the AC planner is not real time.

findings.claim: PaLM-E injects continuous state vectors and image/object features into the LLM embedding space (MLP/affine projections) inside 'multi-modal sentences' with referable entity tokens ('Object j is <obj_j>'), scaling to 562B; 562B loses only 3.9% NLG vs 87.3% for 12B.
findings.source_title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
findings.numbers: 12B (8B+4B ViT), 84B (62B+22B), 562B (540B+22B); TAMP 1% data (320 ex): OSRT 82.5%/76.2% vs ViT-4B single-robot 30.6%/32.9%; Language-Table 80% with 40 demos vs 50%; forgetting 3.9% (562B) vs 87.3% (12B); no code/weights.
findings.relevance: Template for state-as-embedding tokens alongside text and per-entity slots with IDs (owner/person/object) in the state stream.

findings.claim: LEO serializes system message + 2D egocentric tokens + one 3D token per object (up to 60) + instruction, discretizes actions into bins mapped to least-used SentencePiece tokens, trains Vicuna-7B with ~142M LoRA params on ~1M align + ~540K instruct samples; ObjNav success only 23.1.
findings.source_title: An Embodied Generalist Agent in 3D World (LEO), ICML 2024; code/data at embodied-generalist.github.io
findings.numbers: up to 60 objects, 1 token each; Vicuna-7B, ~142M tuned; LEO-align ~1M (660K captioning, 354K referring, 20K scene), LEO-instruct ~540K, 8 task types; ObjNav MP3D 23.1 success / 15.2 SPL; CLIPort 98.8% seen / 75.2% unseen.
findings.relevance: One-token-per-entity serialization and rare-token action vocabulary are directly reusable; weak navigation numbers argue for keeping body navigation in the RL/planner lane.

findings.claim: Octo is a 27M/93M transformer policy that tokenizes task (16 T5 tokens), observations (256 + 64 image patch tokens, proprio) and learned readout tokens under a block-wise causal mask, predicts action chunks with a diffusion head, and fine-tunes to new sensors/action spaces with ~100 demos in <5 h on an A5000; CC BY 4.0.
findings.source_title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy; octo-models.github.io
findings.numbers: Octo-Small 27M, Octo-Base 93M; 800k trajectories from 25 OXE datasets; t5-base 111M -> 16 task tokens; 256 third-person + 64 wrist image tokens; readout tokens not attended by obs/task tokens; 20 diffusion steps; ~100 demos, <5 h on NVIDIA A5000; 9 setups at 4 institutions; CC BY 4.0.
findings.relevance: The concrete blueprint for a small trainable behavior transformer that reads heterogeneous per-tick observation tokens (add audio-event and owner-state tokenizers) and emits actions via readout tokens; desktop-trainable and Orin-deployable at this size.

findings.claim: RT-2 encodes robot actions as 8 integers each in 256 bins as text tokens; the 55B model runs at 1-3 Hz and the 5B at ~5 Hz from a multi-TPU cloud service; unseen-object success 70%/62% vs RT-1 31%/43% over ~6,000 trials.
findings.source_title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control; robotics-transformer2.github.io
findings.numbers: 8 dims x 256 bins; PaLI-X integers up to 1000 have unique tokens, PaLM-E overwrites 256 least-used tokens; sizes 5B/55B PaLI-X, 12B PaLM-E; 55B at 1-3 Hz, 5B ~5 Hz (cloud TPUs); ~6,000 eval trajectories; unseen objects 70%/62% vs 31%/43%; symbols 82% vs 16%; no code/weights.
findings.relevance: Establishes actions-as-text-tokens and the 1-5 Hz rate band for VLM-scale semantic decisions, i.e. the rate of Parcel's semantic lane.

findings.claim: Embodied chain-of-thought (TASK/PLAN/SUBTASK/MOVE/GRIPPER/VISIBLE OBJECTS) raises OpenVLA-7B success from 44% to 66% on generalization tasks with no new robot data, at the cost of 350 vs 7 tokens per timestep; async execution recovers +40% speed at 65%.
findings.source_title: Robotic Control via Embodied Chain-of-Thought Reasoning (ECoT)
findings.numbers: OpenVLA 44% +/- 3.9 -> ECoT 66% +/- 3.8 (RT-2-X 47%); 7 -> 350 tokens/step; Bridge v2 >2.5M transitions annotated over 7 days; 5-step sync +24% speed at 72%; async +40% at 65% (2x compute); human language feedback +48%; CC BY 4.0.
findings.relevance: Structured intermediate state helps a lot, but 50x tokens per step is unaffordable at 5 Hz, so use a compact <=8-token reasoning slot (goal, target entity, mood) instead of free-form CoT.

findings.claim: ELLM captions the agent's state to text (objects seen, inventory, health; object-receptacle relations), asks Codex for goals, and rewards transitions whose caption matches a goal at SentenceBERT similarity > 0.99, improving common-sense behavior coverage during pretraining.
findings.source_title: Guiding Pretraining in Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models (ELLM), ICML 2023
findings.numbers: Codex LLM; similarity threshold 0.99; goal-suggestion caching; ~15% higher ground-truth achievement coverage and 2-3x sample efficiency per the fetched summary; Crafter and Housekeep; code released.
findings.relevance: The caption-the-state / LLM-proposes-goals / reward-on-match loop is how Parcel's text model can shape socially meaningful goals ('re-establish eye contact', 'acknowledge the joke') from the state stream.

findings.claim: FAST tokenizes 1-second action chunks with DCT + scale-round + BPE, compressing 50 Hz actions 13.2x (700 -> 53 tokens) where naive binning fails completely; FAST+ is a universal tokenizer trained on ~1M chunks.
findings.source_title: FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models
findings.numbers: BridgeV2 5 Hz 35->20 tokens; DROID 15 Hz 105->29; bussing 20 Hz 140->28; T-shirt 50 Hz 700->53; up to 50 Hz; FAST+ on ~1M 1-s chunks; up to 5x faster training than diffusion VLAs at 10k h.
findings.relevance: Keeps Parcel's 50 Hz body-intent (velocity-bin ACT tokens) at ~20-50 tokens per second inside the behavior model's output stream.

findings.claim: GR00T N1 is a jointly trained dual-system VLA: a 1.34B Eagle-2 VLM at 10 Hz and a flow-matching diffusion transformer at 120 Hz (16-action chunks in 63.9 ms on an L40), 2.2B total, with embodiment-specific MLPs for state/action; open checkpoint, data and benchmarks under CC BY 4.0.
findings.source_title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
findings.numbers: System 2 10 Hz on L40; System 1 120 Hz, H=16, K=4 denoise steps; 2.2B params; 63.9 ms per 16-action chunk (bf16, L40); 88 h GR-1 teleop + OXE + 140k AgiBot + 827 h neural video + 780k sim trajectories (6,500 h) + human video; sim RoboCasa 32.1% vs 25.6%, DexMimicGen 66.5% vs 56.1%, GR-1 50.0% vs 32.7%; real 76.8% avg over 8 tasks, 42.6% with 10% data vs 10.2%; CC BY 4.0. Helix (vendor) corroborates: 7B VLM at 7-9 Hz -> 80M policy at 200 Hz via one latent, ~500 h teleop.
findings.relevance: Public evidence for the architecture Parcel should copy: a 2-10 Hz semantic/expressive stream conditioning a fast body lane, trained end-to-end, with per-embodiment state encoders.

findings.claim: Moshi is a 7B full-duplex speech model that processes parallel per-stream tokens at 12.5 Hz (Mimi codec, 1.1 kbps, 8 codebooks of 2048, 17 parallel sequences incl. a time-aligned 'inner monologue' text stream) with 160 ms theoretical / 200 ms practical latency; weights CC-BY 4.0, code MIT/Apache-2.0, 24 GB bf16 or int8/int4.
findings.source_title: Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue; code github.com/kyutai-labs/moshi
findings.numbers: 12.5 Hz frames; 1.1 kbps; Q=8 codebooks x 2048; K=2Q+1=17 streams; Helium 7B (32 layers, dim 4096, 2.1T text tokens); depth transformer 6 layers/1024/16 heads; text-audio delay randomized in [-0.6, +0.6] s pretraining, 0 or 1 step finetune; 7M h audio; 160 ms / 200 ms latency; 80 ms codec latency; 24 GB GPU bf16, int8/int4, MLX on Mac/iPhone.
findings.relevance: Reference design for a full-duplex token stream; adding a body/expression stream as one more parallel sequence with a 1-tick delay is the natural extension of Parcel's existing duplex ACT-token codec.

findings.claim: Qwen2.5-Omni's TMRoPE aligns modalities in time with absolute temporal position IDs at a 40 ms quantum and interleaves audio/video in 2-second chunks with block-wise streaming attention; 7B Thinker + Talker, open weights.
findings.source_title: Qwen2.5-Omni Technical Report
findings.numbers: 1 temporal ID = 40 ms; 2-second interleaving chunks (vision first, audio second); audio 128-mel, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop; 2-second attention blocks; DiT receptive field 4 blocks; Thinker 7B; weights at huggingface.co/Qwen; CC BY 4.0 paper.
findings.relevance: Practical answer to timestamping heterogeneous streams in one transformer: a Parcel 200 ms tick = 5 temporal IDs.

findings.claim: Generative Agents' memory stream stores natural-language records with creation/access timestamps and retrieves by recency (decay 0.995 per game hour) + LLM importance (1-10) + embedding relevance, reflecting when summed importance exceeds 150; the full architecture beat the no-memory ablation by 8 SD in a 100-rater TrueSkill study.
findings.source_title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior; code github.com/joonspk-research/generative_agents (retrieve.py read)
findings.numbers: decay 0.995; importance 1-10; alphas = 1 in paper, code weights gw=[0.5,3,2] recency/relevance/importance, n_count=30; reflection threshold 150 (~2-3/day); plans day->hour->5-15 min; 25 agents; 100 evaluators; TrueSkill 29.89 vs 21.21, d=8.16.
findings.relevance: Cheap three-factor retrieval and importance-triggered reflection are reusable on a local model for Parcel's memory view tokens.

findings.claim: A-MEM's Zettelkasten-style notes (content, timestamp, keywords, tags, contextual description, embedding, links; k=10 linking) reach LoCoMo multi-hop F1 45.85 with GPT-4o-mini vs MemGPT 25.52, and F1 24.32 with Qwen2.5-1.5B vs 4.21, at ~1,200 tokens per memory operation (85-93% fewer than baselines); MIT code with Ollama/vLLM backends.
findings.source_title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents (NeurIPS 2025); code github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem
findings.numbers: 7 note fields; k=10; GPT-4o-mini multi-hop F1 45.85 / BLEU-1 36.67 vs MemGPT 25.52/19.44 vs LoCoMo 18.41/14.77; Qwen2.5-1.5B multi-hop F1 24.32 vs 4.21; ~1,200 tokens/op vs ~16,900; six models incl. Llama 3.2 1B/3B; MIT.
findings.relevance: Shows structured memory works with 1.5B-3B local models within Parcel's 'local models run continuously' budget.

findings.claim: Mem0's extract-consolidate-retrieve memory scores 67.13/51.15/72.93/55.51 (single/multi/open/temporal LLM-judge, GPT-4o-mini) on LoCoMo with ~7k tokens per conversation and 1.44 s p95 total latency vs 17.1 s and ~26k tokens for full context; Apache 2.0 with local-LLM support.
findings.source_title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory; code github.com/mem0ai/mem0
findings.numbers: Mem0 67.13/51.15/72.93/55.51; Mem0-g 65.71/47.19/75.71/58.13; A-Mem 39.79/18.85/54.05/49.91; Zep 61.70/41.35/76.60/49.31; OpenAI 63.79/42.92/62.29/21.71; ~7k tokens (Mem0), ~14k (Mem0-g), Zep >600k, full context ~26k; p95 Mem0 1.440 s (search 0.200 s), Mem0-g 2.590 s, full-context 17.117 s; abstract: +26% vs OpenAI memory, -91% p95 latency, -90% tokens; README Apr 2026 (managed platform) LoCoMo 92.5, LongMemEval 94.4, BEAM-1M 64.1, p50 0.88-1.09 s; Apache 2.0.
findings.relevance: Strongest permissively licensed engineering baseline for the owner store; cross-paper memory numbers disagree (A-MEM's own paper vs Mem0's table), so measure in-house.

findings.claim: LoCoMo (50 conversations, 19.3 sessions, 305 turns, ~9.2k tokens each, 7,512 QA) shows long-context LLMs at 37.8 overall F1 vs humans 87.9, collapsing on temporal (20.3) and adversarial (2.1) questions; RAG over observations reaches 41.4.
findings.source_title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents (LoCoMo)
findings.numbers: 50 convs; 19.3 sessions; 304.9 turns; 9,209 tokens; 7,512 QA: single-hop 2,705 (36%), multi-hop 1,104 (14.6%), temporal 1,547 (20.6%), open-domain 285 (3.9%), adversarial 1,871 (24.9%); human 87.9 overall (95.1/85.8/92.6/75.4/89.4); GPT-3.5-turbo-16K 37.8 (temporal 20.3, adversarial 2.1); RAG top-5 41.4; paper page CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0.
findings.relevance: Temporal ('when did we last...') and abstention ('you never told me') are exactly the companion failure modes to test.

findings.claim: MemoryAgentBench (ICLR 2026) evaluates accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and selective forgetting across long-context LLMs, RAG, and agentic memory (Mem0, Cognee, Zep, MemGPT, MIRIX...); all methods fail multi-hop conflict resolution (<= 7%), best single-hop forgetting is GPT-4o at 60%.
findings.source_title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions (MemoryAgentBench); code github.com/HUST-AI-HYZ/MemoryAgentBench
findings.numbers: AR: SH-Doc 100 q/197K tok, MH-Doc 100 q/421K, LongMemEval S* 300 q/355K, EventQA 500 q/534K; TTL: BANKING77/CLINC150/NLU/TREC 100-200 q, movie rec 200 q/1.44M; LRU: InfBench sum 100 q/172K, DetectiveQA 71 q/124K; SF: FactConsolidation SH 100 q/262K, MH 100 q; best AR GPT-4.1-mini 83.0/66.0/55.7/82.6, HippoRAG-v2 76.0/66.0/50.7; TTL Claude-3.7 97.0 BANKING77, 98.0 CLINC150, GPT-4o 87.6 avg; LRU GPT-4o 77.5 avg; SF single-hop best 60.0% (GPT-4o), multi-hop <= 7% for all; MIT code. LongMemEval (arXiv 2410.10813): 500 q, up to 1.5M tokens, 30% accuracy drop for commercial assistants.
findings.relevance: Load-bearing negative result: no current memory agent reliably overwrites facts when the owner changes their mind, so consent-gated owner facts and preferences need an explicit versioned structured store, not LLM-managed free text.

findings.claim: PersonaMem (20 personas, 180+ histories, 10/20/60 sessions, ~6k queries, 32k-1M tokens) finds frontier LLMs (GPT-4.1, o4-mini, GPT-4.5, o1, Gemini-2.0-Flash) score only ~50% at tracking evolving user preferences with the full history in context; weakest on new-idea suggestion, preference-aligned recommendation, and generalizing reasons to new scenarios.
findings.source_title: Know Me, Respond to Me: Benchmarking LLMs for Dynamic User Profiling and Personalized Responses at Scale (PersonaMem); code github.com/bowen-upenn/PersonaMem
findings.numbers: 20 personas; 180+ histories; 10/20/60 sessions; 15-30 turns/session; 15 topics; ~6k query pairs; contexts ~32k/128k/1M; 7 query types; ~50% overall at 128k for frontier models; Llama-4-Maverick 43%.
findings.relevance: Putting the history in the prompt is not enough for a companion to learn the owner; an explicit updatable preference state plus a learning signal is required.

findings.claim: LaMP's seven personalization tasks with user-based and time-based splits show that retrieving a user's own past items (BM25/Contriever/Recency) improves personalized outputs by 23.5% relative when fine-tuned and 12.2% zero-shot.
findings.source_title: LaMP: When Large Language Models Meet Personalization; lamp-benchmark.github.io
findings.numbers: 7 tasks (3 classification, 4 generation); e.g. product rating 20,000/2,500/2,500, news headlines 12,527/1,925/2,376, tweets 10,437/1,500/1,496; user-based and time-based splits; +23.5% fine-tuned, +12.2% zero-shot (FlanT5-XXL, GPT-3.5).
findings.relevance: Time-based splits are the right protocol for measuring whether Parcel's owner model improves with interaction time; recency retrieval is a cheap strong baseline.

findings.claim: No single temporal tokenization is universally best for event sequences in LLMs: numeric strings, byte-level, calendar tokens, uniform binning and adaptive residual quantization each win depending on whether inter-event gaps are smooth log-normal or spiky; event-aligned dynamic tokenization (Dywave) cuts sensor tokens up to 75% with up to 12% accuracy gains.
findings.source_title: Temporal Tokenization Strategies for Event Sequence Modeling with Large Language Models (with Dywave arXiv 2605.14014 and HT-Transformer arXiv 2508.01474 as companions)
findings.numbers: 5 strategies compared; no quantitative results in abstract; Dywave: up to 12% accuracy, up to 75% fewer input tokens, CC BY 4.0; HT-Transformer: history tokens accumulate prefix state, code on GitHub, no numbers in abstract.
findings.relevance: Parcel's stream has bimodal gaps (200 ms ticks vs minutes idle): use a fixed tick index plus log-bucketed time-since-event tokens, calendar tokens for routines, sparse event tokens on top of the fixed tick, and periodic history/summary tokens.

findings.claim: An MIT-licensed laughter segmenter (Gillick et al., Interspeech 2021; Switchboard + AudioSet) with a 0.5 frame threshold and 0.2 s minimum length is available to turn owner laughter into a per-tick state feature and delayed reward; the README gives no accuracy numbers.
findings.source_title: jrgillick/laughter-detection (Robust Laughter Detection in Noisy Environments, Interspeech 2021)
findings.numbers: threshold default 0.5; min_length 0.2 s; Switchboard training, AudioSet annotations; MIT; PyTorch/librosa.
findings.relevance: Grounds the 'learn to chuckle if the joke was funny' reward: laugh onset within 0.5-3 s after a robot utterance tagged as a joke; must be validated on the XVF3800 array audio on hand.

design_implications: Adopt a two-lane, two-rate architecture with one shared state stream: a trainable 2-10 Hz semantic/expressive model (GR00T N1 10 Hz VLM + 120 Hz motor; Helix 7-9 Hz -> 200 Hz; RT-2 1-5 Hz) emitting body-intent setpoints, expression tokens and gaze targets that condition Parcel's existing 50 Hz body-intent lane; the deterministic safety layer keeps final authority and its veto must be visible in the state stream.

Represent the state as a fixed per-tick frame of heterogeneous tokens (Octo observation tokenizers + readout tokens + block-causal mask; Moshi parallel streams at a fixed frame rate; TMRoPE absolute-time positions at a 40 ms quantum), with continuous channels allowed as MLP embeddings (PaLM-E) or zero-padded/masked vectors (TD-MPC2) rather than forced into text.

Keep the visual channel to ~4 tokens per tick: frozen V-JEPA 2 ViT-B/L pooled features (MIT) or Delta-IRIS-style delta tokens, plus one referable token per entity (owner/person/object with bearing, distance, facing flags) following LEO/PaLM-E.

'Look back at the owner when lost' is first a state-feature problem: the stream must carry localization confidence, owner-visible, owner bearing/distance and time-since-owner-seen; then a DreamerV3/TD-MPC2-class agent can learn the gaze/turn behavior in MuJoCo from a dense re-engagement reward.

'Chuckle when the joke was funny' is a delayed-reward problem: laugh onset (MIT laughter detector on the XVF3800 audio) within 0.5-3 s after a joke-tagged robot utterance is the reward; train the chuckle head as a bandit/RL head on the behavior model and write outcomes into memory as skill outcomes (Voyager pattern; existing skill_outcomes.py).

Do not rely on in-context history for user preferences: PersonaMem ~50% for frontier models at 128k, LoCoMo temporal 20.3 / adversarial 2.1, MemoryAgentBench multi-hop conflict resolution <= 7% for every memory agent. The consent-gated owner model must be an explicit versioned structured store (facts + preference slots); the LLM reads a retrieved summarized view (Generative Agents three-factor scoring; A-MEM/Mem0 notes at ~1.2-7k tokens, MIT/Apache-2.0, local-LLM backends).
Use a compact structured reasoning slot (<= 8 tokens: goal, target entity, mood) instead of free-form embodied chain-of-thought: ECoT's +22 points cost 350 vs 7 tokens per step, unaffordable at 5 Hz.

Compress the action side with FAST (DCT+BPE) if body intent is emitted as tokens at 50 Hz (700 -> 53 tokens per second at 50 Hz), and compress the input side with periodic history/summary tokens (HT-Transformer) and MemGPT-style paging of anything older than ~60 s; budget ~50 in + ~30 out tokens per 200 ms tick = ~24k tokens/min.

Use learned world models for the body lane and for evaluation only: DreamerV3 (MIT, 12M-400M, one A100/run) or TD-MPC2 (MIT, 5M on an 8 GB GPU) train on the desktop against MuJoCo Go2 states now; 1X-style policy ranking with the learned world model is a cheap pre-hardware gate; Cosmos/Genie 3/1XWM are offline-only or unavailable.

Evaluate with the benchmarks' protocols rather than their datasets: LaMP time-based splits for 'does it improve with interaction time', LongMemEval knowledge-update and abstention probes, MemoryAgentBench conflict-resolution probes, and an ECoT-style ablation showing that adding the owner/audio channels raises re-engagement and chuckle-timing accuracy.

trainable_options.name: DreamerV3 (body-lane world-model RL)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Single-configuration model-based RL: RSSM world model with categorical latents, policy trained in imagination; handles image + vector observations, discrete or continuous actions.
trainable_options.license: MIT (code; JAX reimplementation unrelated to Google/DeepMind); paper CC BY 4.0
trainable_options.inputs: Dict of sensory inputs (images, proprio/state vectors); for Parcel: proprio + nav + owner-tracker + audio-event channels as vectors
trainable_options.outputs: Continuous or discrete actions (Parcel: 50 Hz body-intent setpoints or 5 Hz gaze/turn intents)
trainable_options.train_recipe: Online RL in MuJoCo Go2 env with dense re-engagement/command/safety rewards; fixed hyperparameters; the paper trained every agent on one A100, so the RTX 5000 Ada 32 GB suffices for 12M-50M configs
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: Feasible for 12M-50M policies (policy network only at inference); no published Orin numbers

trainable_options.name: TD-MPC2 (body-lane world-model RL / planning)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Decoder-free latent world model with MPPI planning (horizon 3), SimNorm latents, ensemble Q-functions; multi-embodiment via zero-padding, action masking and a 96-D task embedding.
trainable_options.license: MIT
trainable_options.inputs: Proprioceptive state up to 223-D (Dog embodiment) or 64x64 pixels
trainable_options.outputs: Continuous actions (masked per embodiment)
trainable_options.train_recipe: Single-task online RL: ~12 GB RAM, 8 GB GPU; multitask offline on the 545M-transition dataset needs 128 GB RAM and a 24 GB GPU for 317M; Parcel would train the 5M-19M configs on MuJoCo Go2 state vectors
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: 5M-19M models are small enough for Orin; MPPI planning per step adds compute (6 iterations, horizon 3)

trainable_options.name: Delta-IRIS (discrete token world model)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Discrete autoencoder over per-step deltas (4 tokens/frame) + autoregressive transformer world model + actor-critic trained in imagination.
trainable_options.license: GPL-3.0 (copyleft; a concern for a product codebase)
trainable_options.inputs: 64x64 frames + action tokens (I-tokens, action tokens, delta-tokens interleaved)
trainable_options.outputs: Discrete actions; imagined future delta tokens
trainable_options.train_recipe: Crafter 10M frames; ~10x faster than IRIS (20 vs 2 FPS collection); a Crafter 5M-frame checkpoint on HF
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: 25M is deployable; GPL-3.0 license and pixel-only inputs limit direct use; the delta-token idea is what to reuse

trainable_options.name: Octo-Small / Octo-Base (behavior transformer template)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Transformer policy over task tokens, per-timestep observation tokens and learned readout tokens with a block-causal mask; diffusion action head with action chunking; new sensors added by adding tokenizers.
trainable_options.license: CC BY 4.0
trainable_options.inputs: Language (16 T5 tokens) or goal image; 256 + 64 image patch tokens per step; proprio tokens; for Parcel add audio-event, owner-state and conversation-state tokenizers
trainable_options.outputs: Action chunks via readout tokens (Parcel: expression, gaze, body-setpoint and vocal-cue streams)
trainable_options.train_recipe: Pretrained on 800k OXE trajectories; fine-tune with ~100 demos in <5 h on an A5000; for Parcel: imitation of authored social policies in a scripted 5 Hz social simulator, then RL fine-tune of chuckle/look-back heads with delayed rewards
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: 27M-93M at 5 Hz is realistic on Orin (no published Orin numbers; GR00T's 2.2B runs 16-action chunks in 63.9 ms on an L40)

trainable_options.name: GR00T N1 (dual-system VLA architecture)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Jointly trained System 2 (Eagle-2 VLM, 10 Hz) + System 1 (flow-matching diffusion transformer, 120 Hz) with embodiment-specific state/action MLPs.
trainable_options.license: CC BY 4.0 (paper); checkpoint, data and benchmarks public on GitHub/Hugging Face
trainable_options.inputs: Images + language + embodiment-specific proprio state
trainable_options.outputs: 16-step action chunks at 120 Hz
trainable_options.train_recipe: Mixture of 88 h real teleop + OXE + 140k AgiBot + 827 h neural video + 780k sim trajectories; fine-tuning with 100 demos per task reported; Parcel would reuse the architecture (dual rate + per-embodiment MLPs), not the humanoid weights
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: 63.9 ms per 16-action chunk on an L40 in bf16; Orin would be slower and shares the GPU with the voice stack, so likely reduced-rate only

trainable_options.name: Moshi (full-duplex speech backbone with parallel streams)
trainable_options.what_it_is: 7B Helium temporal transformer + depth transformer over Mimi codec tokens (12.5 Hz, 8 codebooks) with parallel user/system streams and a time-aligned inner-monologue text stream.
trainable_options.license: Weights CC-BY 4.0; code MIT (Python) / Apache-2.0 (Rust)
trainable_options.size_params: 7B (bf16 24 GB; int8/int4 variants; MLX on Mac/iPhone)
trainable_options.inputs: User audio stream tokens (+ its own audio and text streams); Parcel extension: add a state/body stream as extra parallel sequences
trainable_options.outputs: System audio tokens + text inner monologue at 12.5 Hz; 160/200 ms latency
trainable_options.train_recipe: 7M h audio pretraining; fine-tuning a 7B model on the 32 GB desktop would need LoRA/quantization; realistic Parcel path is adding a small adapter/head for a body stream rather than full fine-tuning
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: int8/int4 7B plausible on Orin 64 GB but heavy alongside other models; latency budget 200 ms already consumed by speech

trainable_options.name: V-JEPA 2 encoder (frozen visual state features)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Self-supervised video ViT encoders (and a 300M action-conditioned predictor) from 1M+ hours of video.
trainable_options.license: MIT (majority) + Apache-2.0 files
trainable_options.size_params: ViT-B 80M / ViT-L 300M / ViT-H 600M / ViT-g 1B / ViT-G 2B; AC predictor ~300M
trainable_options.inputs: Video clips (256 or 384 res)
trainable_options.outputs: Feature tokens (Parcel: pooled to 1-4 tokens per tick); V-JEPA 2-AC planning is 16 s/action and not real time
trainable_options.train_recipe: Use frozen; optionally light adapter training on Parcel's camera data
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: ViT-B/L frozen at 2-5 Hz is feasible; ViT-g and the AC planner are not

trainable_options.name: FAST+ action tokenizer
trainable_options.what_it_is: DCT + BPE compression of continuous action chunks into tokens for autoregressive policies.
trainable_options.license: Not stated in fetched content (FAST+ released as a universal tokenizer)
trainable_options.inputs: 1-second chunks of continuous actions at 5-50 Hz
trainable_options.outputs: ~20-53 tokens per chunk (13.2x compression at 50 Hz)
trainable_options.train_recipe: Fit a Parcel-specific FAST tokenizer on the 50 Hz body-intent lane logs, or use FAST+ black-box
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: Trivial (tokenizer)

trainable_options.name: A-MEM / Mem0 (owner memory store)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Structured long-term memory layers (Zettelkasten notes with links; extract-consolidate-retrieve with optional graph) that work with small local LLMs.
trainable_options.license: A-MEM MIT; Mem0 Apache 2.0
trainable_options.size_params: Uses external LLM (works with Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B, Llama 3.2 1B/3B, GPT-4o-mini)
trainable_options.inputs: Dialogue turns / events with timestamps
trainable_options.outputs: Retrieved memory notes (~1.2k tokens/op A-MEM; ~7k tokens/conversation Mem0; p95 1.44 s Mem0)
trainable_options.train_recipe: No training; configure with local Ollama/vLLM backend; evaluate on time-based splits and conflict-resolution probes (both benchmarks show <= 7% multi-hop conflict resolution for all agents, so add explicit versioning)
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: Feasible with a 1.5B-3B local model; store must be versioned and consent-gated

trainable_options.name: NVIDIA Cosmos-Predict1 (offline sim/data asset)
trainable_options.what_it_is: Open-weight video world foundation models and video tokenizers with action-conditioned post-training support.
trainable_options.license: NVIDIA Open Model License (models); Apache 2.0 (code)
trainable_options.inputs: Text and/or video (+ actions after post-training)
trainable_options.outputs: Future video
trainable_options.train_recipe: Post-train Video2World with action control on custom datasets (MuJoCo-rendered Go2 scenes) to generate camera video for tokenizer pretraining
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: Not deployable on Orin; offline desktop use only (7B fits 32 GB for inference)

open_questions: No fetched source trains a behavior model jointly on audio events + conversation state + proprioception; the recommended token schema is a synthesis of Octo/Moshi/TMRoPE/Delta-IRIS/FAST, not a replication of a published result, so it needs an in-house ablation before being trusted.
Orin throughput for a 27-93M Octo-class behavior model at 5 Hz alongside the duplex voice stack is unmeasured; the only public dual-system timing is GR00T N1's 63.9 ms per 16-action chunk on an L40.

Reliability of laughter detection from the XVF3800 mic array at companion distances is untested; the Gillick repo gives no accuracy numbers, and a false-positive rate directly corrupts the 'joke was funny' reward.

Whether an owner-lost re-engagement behavior learned in MuJoCo with an authored visibility model transfers to a real camera/LiDAR owner-tracker is unknown; the same-day rl-env-readiness audit already refuted the current Go2Env as a training substrate.

Memory-system numbers are not comparable across papers (A-MEM's own LoCoMo F1 vs Mem0's judge score for A-MEM differ by ~2x; Mem0's README numbers are for its managed platform), so the owner-store choice should be made on license and local-model support and then measured in-house with time-based splits and conflict-resolution probes.

The 1X claim that a 70%-accurate world model ranks policies correctly 90% of the time (15% true gap) is single-source (vendor page; the PDF did not parse) and was shown on 3 manipulation tasks; whether a Parcel world model reaches even 70% accuracy on social/expressive outcomes is unknown.
Delta-IRIS's 4-tokens-per-frame result is one paper on Crafter at 64x64 under GPL-3.0; a permissively licensed delta tokenizer for Parcel's camera would have to be trained from scratch.

results.claim: DreamerV3 is a single-configuration world-model RL algorithm that outperforms specialized methods across 150+ tasks in 8 domains, with model sizes 12M-400M params, each agent trained on a single A100, and MIT-licensed code; larger models need less interaction to solve a task.
results.evidence_quote: Nature article (reached via the idp.nature.com cookie redirect) and arXiv 2301.04104v2 PDF: "We evaluate the generality of Dreamer across 8 domains—with over 150 tasks—under fixed hyperparameters. ... All Dreamer agents are trained on a single Nvidia A100 GPU each, making it reproducible for many research labs." / "6 model sizes ranging from 12 million to 400 million parameters" / "larger models not only achieve higher scores but also require less interaction to solve a task" / "Source code for Dreamer and all presented experiments is available under an open-source license at https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3" (GitHub repo: "MIT license"). Also: "All the Dreamer agents we trained on Minecraft discover diamonds in 100M environment steps." / "we employ free bits by clipping the dynamics and representation losses below the value of 1 nat" / "symlog squared error", "symexp twohot loss".
results.correction: All numbers verified against the Nature text and the arXiv v2 PDF (Fig. 1: Atari 57 tasks/200M steps, ProcGen 16 tasks, DMLab 30 tasks). The 'MIT' detail comes from the GitHub repo; the Nature text itself says only 'open-source license'. Note the 2023 arXiv v1 used V100s and 5 sizes (8M-200M); the Nature/v2 numbers (A100, 6 sizes 12M-400M) are the ones cited.

results.claim: Octo is a 27M/93M transformer policy that tokenizes task (16 T5 tokens), observations (256 + 64 image patch tokens, proprio) and learned readout tokens under a block-wise causal mask, predicts action chunks with a diffusion head, and fine-tunes to new sensors/action spaces with ~100 demos in <5 h on an A5000; CC BY 4.0.
