results.evidence_quote: "Octo-Small (27M params) and Octo-Base (93M params)" / "produces a sequence of 16 language embedding tokens" (t5-base) / "256 tokens for the 3rd person camera images and 64 tokens for the wrist camera images" / "The attention pattern of the Octo transformer is block-wise masked: observation tokens can only attend causally to tokens from the same or earlier time steps" / "we insert learned readout tokens that attend to observation and task tokens before it in the sequence, but is not attended to by any observation or task token" / "We use a conditional diffusion decoding head to predict continuous, multi-modal action distributions" (20 diffusion steps) / "~100 in-domain demonstrations and finetunes in <5 hours on a NVIDIA A5000 GPU" / "License: CC BY 4.0". Contradicting the proprio detail: "Adding Proprioceptive Inputs: Policies trained with propioceptive observations seemed generally worse, potentially due to a strong correlation between states and future actions." / "* : New observation input (force-torque proprioception)."
results.correction: Every number is correct (27M/93M, 16 T5 tokens, 256+64 image tokens, 20 diffusion steps, ~100 demos, <5 h on A5000, 800k trajectories from 25 OXE datasets, 9 setups at 4 institutions, CC BY 4.0). The one off detail: the pretrained Octo does NOT consume proprioception as a standard observation token — the paper reports proprio inputs made policies generally worse and lists it as a limitation; proprio appears only as an optional *new* observation input added at finetuning time (e.g. force-torque proprioception on the insertion task). State it as: observations = 256 third-person + 64 wrist image tokens (plus optional proprio added during finetuning).

results.claim: GR00T N1 is a jointly trained dual-system VLA: a 1.34B Eagle-2 VLM at 10 Hz and a flow-matching diffusion transformer at 120 Hz (16-action chunks in 63.9 ms on an L40), 2.2B total, with embodiment-specific MLPs for state/action; open checkpoint, data and benchmarks under CC BY 4.0.
results.evidence_quote: Paper: "our publicly released GR00T-N1-2B model has 2.2B parameters in total, with 1.34B in the VLM" / "The System 2 reasoning module is a pre-trained Vision-Language Model (VLM) that runs at 10Hz on an NVIDIA L40 GPU" / "GR00T N1 uses the NVIDIA Eagle-2 VLM ... as the vision-language backbone" / "a Diffusion Transformer, trained with action flow-matching" that "generates closed-loop motor actions at a higher frequency (120Hz)" / "We set H=16", "K=4 inference steps" / "The inference time for sampling a chunk of 16 actions is 63.9ms on an L40 GPU using bf16" / "embodiment-specific encoders and decoders to handle variable state and action dimensions ... an MLP per embodiment to project them to a shared embedding dimension" / "tightly coupled and jointly trained end-to-end" / "Our GR00T-N1-2B model checkpoint, training data, and simulation benchmarks are publicly available". Contradicting the license detail: the arXiv page's "[License: CC BY 4.0]" is the paper's own license; HuggingFace nvidia/GR00T-N1-2B lists "Nvidia License" and the Isaac-GR00T README says "Model weights: NVIDIA Open Model License" with code under "the Apache License, Version 2.0"; only the HF dataset nvidia/PhysicalAI-Robotics-GR00T-X-Embodiment-Sim is "cc-by-4.0".
results.correction: All architecture/perf numbers verified (1.34B VLM, 10 Hz on L40, 120 Hz, H=16, K=4, 63.9 ms bf16 on L40, 2.2B total, Eagle-2, flow-matching DiT, per-embodiment MLPs, jointly trained; data 88 h/140k/827 h/780k-6,500 h; sim 32.1/25.6, 66.5/56.1, 50.0/32.7; real 76.8%, 42.6% vs 10.2%). Licensing is wrong as stated: CC BY 4.0 applies to the arXiv paper and to the released sim dataset; the GR00T-N1-2B checkpoint is under the NVIDIA Open Model License (not CC BY 4.0) and the Isaac-GR00T code is Apache-2.0. Rewrite as: open checkpoint (NVIDIA Open Model License), code (Apache-2.0), sim data/benchmarks (CC BY 4.0).

results.claim: Moshi is a 7B full-duplex speech model that processes parallel per-stream tokens at 12.5 Hz (Mimi codec, 1.1 kbps, 8 codebooks of 2048, 17 parallel sequences incl. a time-aligned 'inner monologue' text stream) with 160 ms theoretical / 200 ms practical latency; weights CC-BY 4.0, code MIT/Apache-2.0, 24 GB bf16 or int8/int4.
results.evidence_quote: Paper: "7B-parameter text LLM" (Helium, 32 layers, dim 4096, 2.1T tokens) / "12.5 frames per second", "1.1kbps", "Q=8 quantizers, each with a codebook size of N_A=2048" / "amounting to a total number of K=2Q+1 streams, with Q=8 in the experiments" (=17) / Inner Monologue: "time-aligned text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens" / "theoretical latency of 160ms, 200ms in practice" / "randomize the delay between the text and audio tokens between -0.6 and +0.6 seconds" / "7 million hours". GitHub README (kyutai-labs/moshi): "The present code is provided under the MIT license for the Python parts, and Apache license for the Rust backend." / "The weights for the models are released under the CC-BY 4.0 license." / "we do not support quantization for the PyTorch version, so you will need a GPU with a significant amount of memory (24GB)." / "MLX: for on-device inference on iPhone and Mac." / "Moshiko for MLX (int4, int8, bf16)", "Moshiko for PyTorch (bf16, int8)".
results.correction: All numbers verified. Note only that the license, 24 GB, int8/int4 and iPhone/Mac MLX details come from the GitHub README (cited in source_title), not the arXiv paper body; the paper itself covers quantization in Sec. 8/Appendix D (e.g. BF16A8 ~15GB vs bf16 24GB). The 200 ms practical latency is measured on an L4 GPU.

results.claim: MemoryAgentBench (ICLR 2026) evaluates accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and selective forgetting across long-context LLMs, RAG, and agentic memory (Mem0, Cognee, Zep, MemGPT, MIRIX...); all methods fail multi-hop conflict resolution (<= 7%), best single-hop forgetting is GPT-4o at 60%.
results.evidence_quote: Paper: "four core competencies essential for memory agents: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and selective forgetting" / "(4) Selective Forgetting (SF): The skill to revise, overwrite, or remove previously stored information when faced with contradictory evidence" / "We observe that all methods fail on the multi-hop situation (with achieving at most 7% accuracy)." / "Only long context agents can achieve fairly reasonable results on single-hop scenarios." Table 2 FactConsolidation-SH (262K tokens): GPT-4o 60.0, HippoRAG-v2 54.0, BM25 48.0, GPT-4o-mini 45.0, Claude-3.7-Sonnet 43.0, ... Mem0 18.0, Cognee 28.0, Zep 7.0, MemGPT 28.0, MIRIX 14.0; FC-MH all methods <= 5.0. Evaluated agents include "Mem0, Cognee, Zep, Self-RAG, MemGPT, MIRIX". GitHub README: "(Jan. 26th, 2026) Our paper is accepted by Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026)."; repository shows MIT license.
results.correction: Verified. Two notes: (a) the ICLR 2026 acceptance is stated on the GitHub README/OpenReview, not on the arXiv v2 page itself; (b) the 60% single-hop figure is the full-length (262K-token) main-table number — the paper's 6K-context ablation (Table 4) reports GPT-4o at 92.0 on FactCon-SH, and a reasoning-model ablation improves SH but 'does not change the conclusion that Selective Forgetting still poses a significant challenge'. Dataset sizes and AR/TTL/LRU headline numbers (GPT-4.1-mini 83.0/66.0/55.7/82.6; HippoRAG-v2 76.0/66.0/50.7; Claude-3.7 97.0/98.0; GPT-4o 87.6 TTL avg, 77.5 LRU avg) match the paper.

sweeps.topic: Vision-language-action (VLA) and behavior foundation models with action-token outputs, evaluated for fine-tuning on one RTX 5000 Ada 32 GB and deployment on Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB for a conversation-driven, full-duplex Unitree Go2 companion dog

findings.claim: LeRobot's hardware guide puts SmolVLA at ~10-16 GB peak VRAM (batch 8, AdamW) while pi0 / pi0_fast / pi05 / xvla and groot need ~24-40 GB ('24 GB tight at BS 1'); a 50-episode, 5-epoch SmolVLA run is ~3-6 h on a 24 GB L4 and pi0/pi05 is ~4-8 h on an A100-40GB at batch 4.
findings.source_title: LeRobot Compute HW Guide
findings.numbers: SmolVLA ~10-16 GB; pi0/pi05/xvla ~24-40 GB; groot/eo1 ~24-40 GB; L4 24GB smolvla BS4 ~3-6 h; A100-40GB pi0/pi05 BS4 ~4-8 h; 4xH100 pi05 5000 steps 3h41m with gradient checkpointing; SmolVLA 4xH100 5000 steps 27m49s
findings.relevance: Decides which VLAs fit the owner's single 32 GB GPU: SmolVLA comfortably, pi0.5/GR00T only at batch 1-2 with checkpointing.

findings.claim: On-robot characterization (SJTU, Apr 2026) measured pi0 end-to-end latency at 920.6 ms on Jetson AGX Orin versus 246 ms on Jetson Thor and 102.3 ms on an RTX 4090 (35.2 ms compiled); it finds a compute-bound VLM phase followed by a memory-bound action-expert phase, and names Orin the cost/energy-optimal device only for sub-1B 'small consumer' models like SmolVLA.
findings.source_title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
findings.numbers: pi0: Orin 920.6 ms, Thor 246 ms (163 compiled, 6.13 Hz), RTX 4090 102.3 ms (35.2 compiled, 28.41 Hz), B60 306.5, Ascend 310P 818; Orin 42 TFLOP/s BF16, 64 GB, 204 GB/s; Thor 258 TFLOP/s, 128 GB, 273 GB/s; V-AEFusion on Orin 920->806 ms (1.14x); pi0.5-droid Franka 95 ms baseline on 4090
findings.relevance: Primary evidence that 3B-class flow VLAs run at ~1 Hz on Orin; sets the semantic-layer rate budget for Parcel.

findings.claim: ELLSA is the first end-to-end full-duplex model that listens, looks, speaks and acts at once: a Self-Attention MoE with a Llama-3.1-8B speech expert and an Emu3-Base action expert whose last 1,024 token IDs are replaced by FAST action tokens; it runs on a 1-second time block (1 s audio in, one frame, 8 text tokens, 1 s speech + actions out), reaches 89.4% LIBERO average (above pi0-FAST 85.5%), supports speaking-while-acting and 94.3% action barge-in, but costs 786-854 ms per block on an A100.
findings.source_title: End-to-end Listen, Look, Speak and Act (ELLSA)
findings.numbers: LIBERO 90.8/95.8/86.4/84.4 avg 89.4%; speaking-while-acting manipulation 93.3/96.6/86.1/73.2; barge-in 94.3%; dialogue turn-taking 100%; per-block latency A100 854 ms S2S / 786 ms S2A (1 s), 455/428 ms (0.48 s block, action success drops to 71.6-85%); LoRA r=256; robot training data 3,386 LIBERO + 1,693 defective samples; Apache-2.0, ckpt tsinghua-ee/ELLSA
findings.relevance: The direct architectural template for the owner's full-duplex ask; its time-block schedule and FAST-token interleaving transfer, its 8B+8B size does not fit Orin.

findings.claim: Quadruped VLAs converged on a 12-dim command action space (vx, vy, wz, 3 gait params, frequency, height, pitch, foot width, foot height, terminate) emitted by an 8B MLLM at 2 Hz (QUART); QUART-Online's VQ 'Action Chunk Discretization' lifts this to 50 Hz and +65% success; MoRE trains the same VLA as a Q-function on 440K sub-optimal auto-collected trajectories and raises real Unitree Go2 success from 0.44 to 0.60.
findings.source_title: MoRE: Unlocking Scalability in Reinforcement Learning for Quadruped Vision-Language-Action Models (with QUAR-VLA arXiv 2312.14457 and QUART-Online arXiv 2412.15576)
findings.numbers: QUART Fuyu-8B, 256 bins, 2 Hz, QUARD 259K sim + 3K real episodes, seen-task success 0.66/0.60/0.53/0.41/0.32/0.12; QUART-Online codebook 512-dim Nq=2, chunks 1/5/10, 50 Hz, success 0.37-0.52 -> 0.68-0.79; MoRE 1,822,405 QUARD + 440,732 QUARD-Auto, Go2 + D435, 0.60 vs 0.44
findings.relevance: Defines the action interface and the offline-RL-from-mixed-data recipe Parcel should adopt above its 50 Hz body-intent lane.

findings.claim: QuadFM is a 20.27-hour, 11,784-clip text-to-motion dataset for quadrupeds with explicitly emotion-labelled behaviors (Happy: dancing/excited; Sad: cautious; greeting, begging, stretching); its MotionGPT3-style generator runs at 2 Hz with a 50 Hz RL tracking policy and achieves <500 ms end-to-end on a Unitree Go2 X with an NVIDIA Orin.
findings.source_title: QuadFM: Foundational Text-Driven Quadruped Motion Dataset
findings.numbers: 11,784 clips, 20.27 h, 3.64M frames @50 Hz, 35,352 texts; generator 2 Hz, tracker 50 Hz; <500 ms e2e on Go2 X + Orin; cloud ASR (Qwen-Omni) adds ~0.5 s; trained ~48 h on one AMD MI308X; human eval 7.98/9 alignment; CC BY 4.0; GitHub placeholder 'will be released soon'
findings.relevance: Shows an emotion-expressive Go2 motion layer running on Orin in real time; the affective categories match Parcel's needs; weights/data not yet public.

findings.claim: openpi releases pi0, pi0-FAST and pi0.5 under Apache-2.0 with a GPU table: inference >8 GB, LoRA fine-tuning >22.5 GB (RTX 4090), full fine-tuning >70 GB (A100-80/H100); base models were pre-trained on 10k+ hours; a PyTorch backend exists since Sep 2025; no Jetson notes.
findings.source_title: Physical-Intelligence/openpi README
findings.numbers: inference >8 GB; LoRA >22.5 GB; full FT >70 GB; 10k+ h pretraining; Apache-2.0
findings.relevance: pi0.5 LoRA is feasible but tight on 32 GB; full fine-tuning is impossible locally.

findings.claim: pi0 is 3.3B (PaliGemma 3B + 300M flow-matching action expert), outputs 50-step chunks at up to 50 Hz with 10 integration steps, was trained on 903M timesteps (10k+ h, 7 robots, 68 tasks), needs 5 h to 100+ h of data per fine-tuned task, and infers in 73 ms on an RTX 4090 (14 ms image, 32 ms forward, 27 ms flow).
findings.source_title: pi0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
findings.numbers: 3.3B; H=50; 50 Hz; 10 steps; 903M timesteps; fine-tune 5-100+ h; 4090 on-board 73 ms, off-board 86 ms; pi0-small 470M
findings.relevance: Canonical continuous-action VLA; its data appetite (hours per task) is far above what Parcel can collect.

findings.claim: FAST tokenizes action chunks with DCT + BPE (two hyperparameters: rounding scale 10, vocab 1024), compressing 700 naive tokens to 53 for 50 Hz t-shirt folding (13.2x) and 35 to 20 for 5 Hz Bridge (1.75x); pi0-FAST trains with 5x fewer GPU-hours than pi0 but infers at ~750 ms per chunk versus ~100 ms for the flow variant; FAST+ was trained on ~1M 1-second chunks and is usable in three lines via HF AutoProcessor.
findings.source_title: FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models
findings.numbers: BridgeV2 5 Hz 35->20; DROID 15 Hz 105->29; bussing 20 Hz 140->28; T-shirt 50 Hz 700->53; 5x fewer GPU-h; ~750 ms/chunk vs ~100 ms; FAST+ 1M chunks; scale 10, vocab 1024
findings.relevance: Drop-in replacement for Parcel's naive velocity-bin ACT codec that keeps actions as language-model tokens.

findings.claim: OpenVLA (7B, MIT) discretizes actions into 256 bins overwriting the 256 least-used Llama tokens, took 21,500 A100-hours to pretrain, runs at ~6 Hz on an RTX 4090 in bf16 (16.8 GB; int8 10.2 GB; int4 7.0 GB with no success loss), and LoRA-fine-tunes (rank 32, 1.4% of params) in 10-15 h on a single A100 with 10-150 demos per task.
findings.source_title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
findings.relevance: Baseline token VLA; too slow per token for a 50 Hz loop and 32 GB is marginal for LoRA.

findings.claim: OpenVLA-OFT swaps the token head for parallel decoding + action chunking + an L1-regression continuous head, raising LIBERO from 76.5% to 97.1% with 26x throughput (0.0729 s per 8-step chunk) and 43x on ALOHA (K=25, 25 Hz) using 20-300 demos per task; the repo states training needs '1-8 GPUs with 27-80 GB' and inference ~16-18 GB.
findings.source_title: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success (OpenVLA-OFT)
findings.numbers: 76.5 -> 97.1%; 26x (K=8) / 43x (K=25); 0.0729 s per chunk; ALOHA demos 20/30/45/300; 8x A100/H100-80GB 50-150K steps; repo 27-80 GB per GPU; inference ~16-18 GB; without FiLM language following drops to 33%; MIT
findings.relevance: Shows chunked continuous heads are 26-43x faster than per-dimension tokens on the same backbone; 27 GB minimum is at the edge of the 32 GB card.

findings.claim: GR00T N1 is a 2.2B dual-system VLA (Eagle-2 VLM 1.34B at 10 Hz on an L40; flow-matching DiT at 120 Hz, 16-step chunks, 4 denoising steps) that samples a chunk in 63.9 ms on an L40 in bf16, was pretrained with ~50,000 H100 GPU-hours on 88 h real + ~827 h neural + 6,500 h sim data, and post-trains with 30/100/300 demos to 76.8% real-robot success vs 46.4% for Diffusion Policy.
findings.source_title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
findings.relevance: Reference dual-rate architecture (System 2 / System 1) that Parcel's semantic layer + 50 Hz intent lane mirrors.

findings.claim: The Isaac-GR00T repo (N1.7 GA, 3B, Cosmos-Reason2-2B backbone) recommends 40 GB+ VRAM for fine-tuning (A6000 'works but may require longer training time'), 16 GB+ for inference explicitly including Jetson AGX Thor/Orin with an official scripts/deployment/orin/install_deps.sh (JetPack 7.2), and ships no LoRA flags or latency table; N1.7 weights are under the NVIDIA Open Model License ('ready for commercial/non-commercial use', H100 TensorRT 27.9 ms / 35.9 Hz) whereas the N1.5/N1.6 weight LICENSE is a non-commercial 'NVIDIA License'.
findings.source_title: NVIDIA Isaac-GR00T README (with GR00T-N1.7-3B and GR00T-N1.6-3B model cards)
findings.numbers: 3B; fine-tune 40 GB+; inference 16 GB+; N1.7 DiT 16 layers vs 32 in N1.6; tutorials 3-5 episodes; single-GPU example batch 32, 2000 steps; N1.7 H100 TRT 27.9 ms / 35.9 Hz; code Apache-2.0
findings.relevance: Only 3B-class VLA with an official Orin path; 32 GB is below the fine-tuning recommendation; only N1.7 is commercially usable.

findings.claim: SmolVLA is a 450M VLA (100M flow-matching expert, first 16 layers of SmolVLM-2, 50-action chunks) pretrained on 481 community datasets (22.9K episodes, 10.6M frames, ~30k GPU-h on 4 GPUs); LeRobot docs recommend ~50 episodes (25 'was not enough'), 20k fine-tuning steps take ~4 h on one A100, inference needs ~2 GB (pi0: 14 GB), and asynchronous inference is ~30% faster (19 vs 9 pick-place cycles).
findings.source_title: SmolVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Affordable and Efficient Robotics (with LeRobot smolvla and async docs)
findings.numbers: 450,046,176 params; 481 datasets, 22.9K episodes, 10.6M frames; 200k steps batch 256; ~50 episodes; 20k steps ~4 h A100; ~2 GB inference; LIBERO 87.3%; SO-100 real 78.3%; async +30%, 19 vs 9 cycles; actions_per_chunk 50, chunk_size_threshold 0.5-0.7; LeRobot Apache-2.0
findings.relevance: The one VLA that fits the 32 GB card with headroom and has an Orin-class footprint; its ~50-episode fine-tuning quantum is achievable in sim.

findings.claim: NaVILA (RSS 2025) drives a Unitree Go2/H1/Booster T1 by having an 8B VILA VLM emit mid-level language actions ('move forward 75 cm', 'turn right 30 deg') at ~1 Hz on an RTX 4090 (W4A16 8.6 GB, +40% speed) into a 50 Hz Isaac-Lab PPO locomotion policy (60K FPS on a 4090), reaching 88% real-world success on 25 instructions; checkpoint and code are Apache-2.0, locomotion code MIT.
findings.source_title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
findings.numbers: VILA 8B Llama3; ~1 Hz on 4090; W4A16 8.6 GB; PPO 60K FPS; 2K YouTube videos -> 20K trajectories; R2R val-unseen 54.0%, RxR 44.0%; VLN-CE-Isaac Go2 50.2%; real 88%/25; ckpt a8cheng/navila-llama3-8b-8f
findings.relevance: Proves a 1 Hz language-action layer over a 50 Hz RL controller on the exact robot; inference was off-board, so Orin would be slower than 1 Hz.

findings.claim: Uni-Mo generates 7,488 language-annotated Go2 motions (18.5 h) from LLM prompts via a fine-tuned video-diffusion model and 3D lifting, then trains per-motion PPO tracking policies (MLP 512/256/128, 50 Hz PD, 4,096 envs on one RTX 3090, up to 3,000 iterations) that reach 97.6% in MuJoCo and 96.7% on a real Unitree Go2 over 392 motions x 5 trials.
findings.source_title: Unleashing Infinite Motion: Scaling Expressive Quadrupedal Motion via Generative Video Priors (Uni-Mo / Quad-Imaginarium)
findings.numbers: 7,488 motions, 18.5 h; 19-D state; 50 Hz; MLP (512,256,128); PPO 4,096 envs on one 3090; sim 97.6%; real 96.7% (392 x 5); video model 56 H20 GPUs; CC BY 4.0 dataset
findings.relevance: A consumer-GPU recipe for an expressive Go2 motion library with tracking policies that Parcel's MuJoCo env can host.

findings.claim: The pi0.6 model card (Nov 17 2025) describes a Gemma3-4B + SigLIP-400M backbone with an 860M action expert trained with knowledge insulation (backbone predicts FAST tokens, expert predicts continuous actions), optional 'conditioning metadata in the prompt', and 63 ms per chunk on an H100 with 5 denoising steps and 3 cameras; pi*0.6's RECAP RL post-training more than doubles throughput and halves failures; the weights are not in openpi and a release request is unanswered.
findings.source_title: pi0.6 Model Card (Physical Intelligence)
findings.numbers: Gemma3 4B + SigLIP 400M + 860M expert (~5B); 4 images 448x448; 5 denoise steps; 63 ms H100; RECAP >2x throughput, >=2x fewer failures; not open
findings.relevance: State of the art for metadata-conditioned VLAs and RL post-training, but closed; only the design ideas transfer.

findings.claim: On Jetson AGX Thor, pi0.5 infers in ~132 ms (PyTorch BF16) and ~49 ms with TensorRT FP8+NVFP4 (~2.7x) per NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab tutorial (Orin not covered); a community forum post (May 2026) reports pi0.5 44 ms (23 Hz), pi0 46 ms, GR00T N1.6 41-45 ms on Thor and 13-18 ms on an RTX 5090; an openpi issue reports a 'hacky' pi0.5-droid pipeline on Jetson Orin at 1.2 s round trip.
findings.source_title: OpenPi pi0.5 on Jetson Thor (Jetson AI Lab) + NVIDIA forum post 368788 + openpi issue #826
findings.numbers: Thor pi0.5 ~132 ms BF16 / ~49 ms TRT; forum: pi0.5 Thor 44 ms (23 Hz), 5090 17.58 ms (57 Hz); pi0 Thor 46 ms; GR00T N1.6 Thor 45/41 ms, 5090 13.08/12.53 ms; pi0-FAST Thor 8.1 ms/token; Orin pi0.5 1.2 s round trip
findings.relevance: Thor is 5-20x faster than Orin on every 3B VLA; the Orin design must stay sub-1B or 1-2 Hz.

findings.claim: LiteVLA-Edge runs a SmolVLM-256M-backbone VLA quantized to Q4_K_M (GGUF) at a mean end-to-end latency of 150.5 ms (std 0.125 ms) on a Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB.
findings.source_title: LiteVLA-Edge: Quantized On-Device Multimodal Control for Embedded Robotics
findings.numbers: SmolVLM-256M; 42 layers; 4-bit Q4_K_M; 150.5 ms mean, 0.125 ms std; Orin 64 GB; no success-rate comparison reported
findings.relevance: Only primary sub-200 ms VLA latency on the exact Orin variant; it required a 256M backbone.

findings.claim: Gemini Robotics On-Device (Jun 24 2025) adapts with 'as few as 50 to 100 demonstrations' and ships a MuJoCo SDK, but both it and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 (Jul 30 2026; SO101 53.3% vs 6.7%, Dexmate 75.6% vs 33.3%) are distributed only to trusted testers with no downloadable weights or license.
findings.source_title: Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 Model Card (with the Jun 2025 On-Device blog)
findings.numbers: 50-100 demos; ALOHA, Franka FR3, Apollo; On-Device 2: SO101 53.3% vs 6.7%; Dexmate 75.6% vs 33.3%; trusted testers only
findings.relevance: Not obtainable for Parcel; confirms the 50-100 demo fine-tuning quantum across vendors.

findings.claim: Figure Helix splits control into a 7B open-weight VLM (System 2) at 7-9 Hz and an 80M cross-attention transformer (System 1) at 200 Hz over a 35-DoF action space, trained on ~500 h of teleop and run onboard on dual low-power embedded GPUs with S2 as an asynchronous background process.
findings.source_title: Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control
findings.numbers: S2 7B @ 7-9 Hz; S1 80M @ 200 Hz; 35-DoF; ~500 h; dual embedded GPUs; closed
findings.relevance: Industry confirmation of the slow-semantic / fast-motor split at the ratios Parcel already uses.

findings.claim: LAPA learns a discrete latent action space (vocab 8, length 4) from video without action labels and pretrains a 7B VLA in 272 H100-hours (8 H100 x 34 h), 30-40x cheaper than OpenVLA, beating it 50.1% vs 43.9% on real tabletop tasks; weights are MIT but fine-tuning used 4x A100-80GB.
findings.source_title: LAPA: Latent Action Pretraining from Videos
findings.numbers: codebook 8^4; LWM-Chat-1M 7B; 272 H100-h; 30-40x cheaper than 21,500 A100-h; 50.1% vs 43.9%; fine-tune 4x A100-80GB; MIT
findings.relevance: Cheapest published route to a pretrained action prior; the latent-action idea could be applied to dog videos, but the 7B backbone is too large for the target hardware.

findings.claim: UniAct-0.5B (LLaVA-OneVision-0.5B) maps 28 embodiments onto a shared 256x128 universal action codebook with per-robot MLP heads, adapts to a new robot with 100 demos in 1 h on 4 A100s, and beats OpenVLA-7B on WidowX; the license is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
findings.source_title: Universal Actions for Enhanced Embodied Foundation Models (UniAct)
findings.numbers: 0.5B; codebook 256x128; 1M demos / 28 embodiments; 100 demos, 4 A100, 1 h; Libero decoder 61.3%, Bridge 63.3%; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
findings.relevance: Smallest universal-action-token model, but the non-commercial license and the missing quadruped embodiment limit it.

findings.claim: Being-H0 releases 1B/8B/14B InternVL3-based VLAs under MIT with an 8-layer grouped-residual hand-motion tokenizer (codebooks 4096, millimeter-level reconstruction) pretrained on UniHand (150M samples, 1,100+ h of human video) and post-trained with 50-100 teleop trajectories per task.
findings.source_title: Being-H0: Vision-Language-Action Pretraining from Large-Scale Human Videos
findings.numbers: 1B/8B/14B; UniHand 150M samples, 1,100+ h, 11 sources, 2.5M instruction points; GRQ 8 layers, codebooks 4096; 50-100 trajectories; MIT; released 2025-08-02
findings.relevance: Smallest MIT-licensed VLA with a learned motion tokenizer; hand-centric, so the tokenizer would need retraining on dog motion.

findings.claim: RT-2 represents actions as 256-bin integer text tokens and runs its 55B PaLI-X variant at 1-3 Hz and the 5B variant at ~5 Hz on a multi-TPU cloud service; it doubled emergent-generalization success (62% vs 32% for RT-1) over ~6k trials and is closed.
findings.source_title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
findings.numbers: 5B / 12B / 55B; 256 bins; 55B 1-3 Hz, 5B ~5 Hz cloud TPU; ~6k trials; 62% vs 32%
findings.relevance: Canonical origin of action-as-text-tokens; establishes why per-dimension token decoding is rate-limited.

findings.claim: Xiaomi-Robotics-0 (Feb 2026, Apache-2.0) is a 4.7B Qwen3-VL-4B + DiT flow-matching VLA trained for asynchronous execution with a training-time real-time-chunking Lambda-shape mask, inferring in 80 ms on an RTX 4090 and reaching 98.7% on LIBERO.
findings.source_title: Xiaomi-Robotics-0: An Open-Sourced Vision-Language-Action Model with Real-Time Execution
findings.numbers: 4.7B; 80 ms 4090; ~200M timesteps + 80M VL samples; LIBERO 98.7%; Apache-2.0; VRAM for fine-tuning unstated
findings.relevance: Newest open flow VLA with built-in async-execution training; too large for Orin real-time, VRAM for 32 GB fine-tuning unverified.

findings.claim: BFM-Zero trains a 31.9M-parameter promptable behavior foundation model (latent 256, forward-backward representation) purely in IsaacLab (1024 envs, 192M steps, 200 Hz sim / 50 Hz control) on LAFAN1's 4,040 motions and deploys zero-shot motion tracking, goal reaching and reward optimization on a real Unitree G1 at 50 Hz.
findings.source_title: BFM-Zero: A Promptable Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control Using Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
findings.numbers: actor 31.9M (6-block, 2048); latent 256; LAFAN1 4,040 motions; IsaacLab 1024 envs; 192M env steps / 3M updates; 50 Hz on G1
findings.relevance: Shows a tiny sim-trained latent policy can be prompted by reward/goal/motion and transfers to real hardware; the recipe for Parcel's expressive 50 Hz layer.

design_implications: Keep Parcel's 50 Hz body-intent lane + deterministic safety layer as 'System 1' and add a 1-2 Hz semantic VLA above it; every quadruped VLA (QUART 2 Hz, NaVILA 1 Hz, QuadFM 2 Hz generator) and every dual-system humanoid stack (GR00T 10/120 Hz, Helix 7-9/200 Hz) uses this split, and primary Orin numbers (pi0 920 ms; pi0.5 1.2 s round trip) rule out 3B VLAs in the fast loop.

Define the action interface as a QUART-style 12-dim command chunk (vx, vy, wz, gait params, frequency, height, pitch, foot params, terminate) extended with expressive-motion ids, tokenized with FAST (DCT+BPE, 2-13x fewer tokens than binning, three-line HF integration) so actions stay in the same token stream as speech/text; if the semantic model is flow-based instead, expose a QUART-Online VQ chunk codebook to the intent lane.

Start the trainable semantic layer from SmolVLA (450M, Apache-2.0 code, ~10-16 GB at BS 8, ~4 h per 20k steps, ~2 GB at inference): it is the only VLA that fits the 32 GB card with headroom for Parcel's other resident local models and has an Orin-class footprint; pi0.5 LoRA (>22.5 GB) and GR00T N1.7 (40 GB+ recommended, commercial license, official Orin script) are upgrade paths that need a bigger training box.

Implement full duplex as ELLSA-style time-block scheduling (1 s block: 1 s audio in, one frame, few text tokens, 1 s speech + action tokens out; barge-in cancels the action chunk) rather than as one giant model; run the speech expert on the hosted Realtime API within the $300/mo budget and only the action expert locally, since ELLSA's 8B+8B experts cost 786-854 ms per block on an A100.

Feed 'state of the world' as prompt metadata tokens (owner-model facts, affect estimate, ASR text, owner pose from LiDAR/camera, recent event history), the mechanism pi0.6 ('conditioning metadata in the prompt') and ELLSA (speech + frame + text in one stream) use; do not try to make the VLA infer these from pixels alone.

Learn 'chuckle if the joke was funny' and 'look back when lost' as reward-conditioned behaviors: warm-start with 50-100 scripted sim episodes per behavior (the fine-tuning quantum across SmolVLA, Gemini On-Device, Being-H0, GR00T), then run MoRE-style offline RL (VLA as Q-function on mixed-quality autonomous rollouts; 0.44->0.60 on a real Go2) or RECAP-style advantage conditioning, with an external funniness signal (laughter detector / LLM judge / consent-gated owner feedback) and a geometric owner-reacquired reward.

Build the expressive 50 Hz motion library with the Uni-Mo/QuadFM/BFM-Zero recipe: per-motion or latent-conditioned PPO tracking policies trained in MuJoCo/Isaac Lab (4,096 envs on one consumer GPU, 96.7% real Go2 success reported), with QuadFM's affective categories (happy/excited, sad/cautious, greeting, begging, stretching) as the token vocabulary; this replaces the fixed command list and needs no teleoperation.

Licensing filter: prefer openpi (Apache-2.0), OpenVLA/OFT (MIT), LeRobot/SmolVLA (Apache-2.0), Being-H0 (MIT), LAPA (MIT), GR00T N1.7 (NVIDIA Open Model License); avoid GR00T N1.5/N1.6 weights, UniAct and Meta Motivo (non-commercial) if Parcel might ever ship; RT-2, Helix, Gemini On-Device and pi0.6 are unobtainable.

Hardware decision for the owner: Thor is 5-20x faster than Orin on every 3B VLA measured (pi0.5 44-49 ms vs ~1 s); if the semantic layer must exceed ~2 Hz on the dog, plan a Thor upgrade; on Orin the design must stay sub-1B (SmolVLA-class; LiteVLA-Edge 150 ms with a 256M backbone) or accept 1-2 Hz.

open_questions: No primary latency number exists for SmolVLA or GR00T N1.6/N1.7 on Jetson AGX Orin (only Thor, 4090, 5090 and a 256M-backbone Orin figure); a 1-day Orin benchmark of SmolVLA is the cheapest way to close this.

Whether GR00T N1.7 (3B) fine-tunes at all on a 32 GB GPU: the README recommends 40 GB+ and documents no LoRA/freeze flags; LeRobot's 24-40 GB envelope suggests batch 1-2 with checkpointing might work.

Whether openpi's '>22.5 GB' pi0.5 LoRA figure leaves enough of the 32 GB card for Parcel's other resident local models (voice codec, owner model) during a training run, or whether training must be scheduled when they are stopped.
QuadFM's dataset and generator weights are not yet released (GitHub placeholder); Uni-Mo's Quad-Imaginarium dataset is released but the code status was not confirmed in the fetched text.

No quadruped VLA in the fetched literature is conditioned on conversational or affective state; the reward signal for 'the joke was funny' (laughter detection, LLM judge, or consent-gated owner feedback) has no published precedent and must be designed and validated in sim first.
ELLSA has not been run on any Jetson in the fetched sources; whether its 1 s time-block schedule survives replacing the 8B experts with sub-1B ones is untested.

Web-search budget expired before checking for a community SmolVLA-on-Jetson benchmark, a primary 'EdgeVLA' source, or a GR00T N1.5 Orin latency report; those figures (including the ~2 Hz OpenVLA-on-Orin claim seen only in a secondary blog) remain unverified and were not cited.

results.claim: LeRobot's hardware guide puts SmolVLA at ~10-16 GB peak VRAM (batch 8, AdamW) while pi0 / pi0_fast / pi05 / xvla and groot need ~24-40 GB ('24 GB tight at BS 1'); a 50-episode, 5-epoch SmolVLA run is ~3-6 h on a 24 GB L4 and pi0/pi05 is ~4-8 h on an A100-40GB at batch 4.

(Peak VRAM (BS 8, AdamW)) ... | Single L4 / A10G (24 GB) | `smolvla` | 4 | ~3–6h | ... | Single A100 40 GB | `pi0` / `pi05` | 4 | ~4–8h | ... 4×H100 80 GB cluster, 5000 steps, batch 32: `smolvla` 27m 49s ... `pi05` 3h 41m ... `gradient_checkpointing=true`
results.correction: All numbers match. Two small precision notes: the parenthetical '24 GB tight at BS 1' is attached only to the Large VLA row (pi0/pi0_fast/pi05/xvla/wall_x); the groot/eo1 'Multimodal' row says just 'A100 40 GB+'. The L4 SmolVLA ~3-6 h figure is at batch 4 (claim omits the batch), and the doc stresses these are 'indicative' order-of-magnitude figures (±50%).

results.claim: On-robot characterization (SJTU, Apr 2026) measured pi0 end-to-end latency at 920.6 ms on Jetson AGX Orin versus 246 ms on Jetson Thor and 102.3 ms on an RTX 4090 (35.2 ms compiled); it finds a compute-bound VLM phase followed by a memory-bound action-expert phase, and names Orin the cost/energy-optimal device only for sub-1B 'small consumer' models like SmolVLA.

Table 1. π0-related data presented in the Leaderboard: 4090 ... 102.3; Thor ... 246.0; Orin 64 204 1999 1.866 920.6; B60 ... 306.5; 310p ... 818.0 ... Table 3: RTX 4090 102.3 / 35.2 / 2.90× / 28.41 Hz; Jetson Thor 246.0 / 163.0 / 1.51× / 6.13 Hz ... 'We classify VLA models into two tiers using a 1B-parameter threshold: Small Consumers (e.g., ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA) and Big Consumers (e.g., Gr00t, π0, π0.5, OpenVLA)' ... 'CE Sorted (Cost-Energy Priority): ... Here, the Orin is optimal for small consumers like SmolVLA, whereas the 310P proves superior for heavier workloads like Gr00t and π0.' ... results.correction: Every number checks out (fetched via the PDF text; the abstract page confirms 27 Apr 2026). One nuance: the 'Orin is optimal for small consumers like SmolVLA' statement is specifically under the CE-sorted (cost-energy priority, latency not critical) ranking; under the all-round CET ranking the paper picks Thor for SmolVLA, and under energy-only priority for π0 it lists 'Jetson Thor, followed by AGX Orin'.

results.claim: ELLSA is the first end-to-end full-duplex model that listens, looks, speaks and acts at once: a Self-Attention MoE with a Llama-3.1-8B speech expert and an Emu3-Base action expert whose last 1,024 token IDs are replaced by FAST action tokens; it runs on a 1-second time block (1 s audio in, one frame, 8 text tokens, 1 s speech + actions out), reaches 89.4% LIBERO average (above pi0-FAST 85.5%), supports speaking-while-acting and 94.3% action barge-in, but costs 786-854 ms per block on an A100.
results.evidence_quote: 'ELLSA ... is the first full-duplex, end-to-end model that simultaneously perceives and generates across vision, text, speech, and action within a single architecture ... a novel SA-MoE architecture (Self-Attention Mixture-of-Experts)' ... 'ELLSA operates on a one-second time block, within which it processes one second of speech input and a single video frame, generates eight tokens of text output (or a single <silence> token ...), and produces one second of speech and action output.' ... 'The LLM backbone is LLama-3.1-8B-Instruct ... LoRA applied at rank 256' ... 'The backbone is Emu3-Base, the final 1,024 token IDs of which are replaced with FAST tokens to enable action prediction.' ... Table 2: π0-FAST 96.4% 96.8% 88.6% 60.2% 85.5%; ELLSA 90.8% 95.8% 86.4% 84.4% 89.4% ... Table 3(c) speaking-while-acting: General question 100.0% / Interruptive command 94.3% / Silence 100.0% ... Table 4(b) 93.3% 96.6% 86.1% 73.2% ... Table 9(d) Per-time-block latency (A100): 1s 854ms speech-to-speech / 786ms speech-to-action; 0.48s 455ms / 428ms ... training data: robot manipulation LIBERO 3386, defective instruction rejection 1693
results.correction: All figures verified in the v2 PDF (20 Apr 2026). Minor notes: the 94.3% is the 'Interruptive command' success rate within the speaking-while-acting task (Table 3c), i.e. the action barge-in case; latency numbers come from Appendix Table 9(d) and the authors note both configurations complete within their block. The Apache-2.0 license and 'tsinghua-ee/ELLSA' checkpoint are not in the paper text but are confirmed on the GitHub ELLSA branch (License Apache 2.0 badge, ELLSA checkpoint from tsinghua-ee/ELLSA) and the Hugging Face model card (18B params, BF16 safetensors); training code is still 'Coming soon'.

results.claim: Quadruped VLAs converged on a 12-dim command action space (vx, vy, wz, 3 gait params, frequency, height, pitch, foot width, foot height, terminate) emitted by an 8B MLLM at 2 Hz (QUART); QUART-Online's VQ 'Action Chunk Discretization' lifts this to 50 Hz and +65% success; MoRE trains the same VLA as a Q-function on 440K sub-optimal auto-collected trajectories and raises real Unitree Go2 success from 0.44 to 0.60.
results.evidence_quote: MoRE: 'a_t is de-tokenized into 12-dimensional discretized robot commands: [v_x, v_y, ω_z, θ_1, θ_2, θ_3, f, h_z, φ, s_y, h_z^f, T]' ... 'MoRE employs a RL-based training objective to train our model as a Q-function' ... 'includes a total of 440,732 vision-language-action sets with all data sourced from QUARD-Auto' ... 'we exclusively used failure data from the QUARD-Auto dataset' ... 'TABLE I: Overall performance. We evaluate 25 episodes per task for the final checkpoint on 6 challenging tasks from QUARD and report the success rates.' QUART (8B) ... avg 0.44; MoRE (9.82B) ... avg 0.60 ... Real world: 'The robot used to collect the trajectory data is Unitree Go2 ... RealSense d435' ... 'MoRE successfully completed tasks such as go to the computer, crawl under the bar, and unload the yellow ball in real-world scenarios' (no real-world success rates). QUAR-VLA (2312.14457): 'discretize all continuous dimensions into 256 uniformly sized bins' ... 'simulation data (259K episodes) and a small amount of real-world data (3K episodes)' ... 'For QUART, the inference time could get 2Hz' ... fuyu-8b. QUART-Online (2412.15576): 'achieving real-time inference at 50Hz in sync with the underlying controller frequency' ... 'boosting the success rate across various tasks by 65%' ... codebook '512 dimensions and 512 quantizers', 'Nq=2'.
results.correction: The action space, QUART (Fuyu-8B, 256 bins, 2 Hz, 259K sim + 3K real), QUART-Online (ACD, 50 Hz, +65%, 512-dim codebook Nq=2, 0.37/0.52 -> 0.68/0.79) and MoRE's Q-function/440,732-sample QUARD-Auto facts all check out. The error is the venue of the 0.44 -> 0.60 result: it is MoRE's Table I SIMULATION average (25 episodes per task on 6 QUARD sim tasks; QUART 0.44 vs MoRE 0.60), not a real-Unitree-Go2 rate. The real-robot section (Go2 + RealSense D435, fine-tuned on a small real dataset) reports only qualitative successes on 'go to', 'crawl', 'unload' with no numbers. Also '440K trajectories' should read 440,732 vision-language-action sets (samples), described as failure data; MoRE itself is 9.82B (Fuyu-8B + MoE-LoRA), not exactly 'the same' 8B VLA.

results.claim: QuadFM is a 20.27-hour, 11,784-clip text-to-motion dataset for quadrupeds with explicitly emotion-labelled behaviors (Happy: dancing/excited; Sad: cautious; greeting, begging, stretching); its MotionGPT3-style generator runs at 2 Hz with a 50 Hz RL tracking policy and achieves <500 ms end-to-end on a Unitree Go2 X with an NVIDIA Orin.

'We initialize the motion generator with MotionGPT3' ... 'The motion generator runs at 2Hz to produce motion commands, while the generic locomotion controller executes them at 50Hz for stable tracking.' ... 'we train πϕ with PPO using a tracking-style reward' ... 'end-to-end latency below 500 ms for responsive language-guided interaction' ... 'Our end-to-end real-robot deployment runs on a Unitree GO2 X quadruped, where both the motion generator and the low-level controller are deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin.' ... 'ASR is performed in the cloud using Qwen-Omni ... the overall latency from speech input to motion execution is approximately 0.5s' ... 'single AMD MI308X GPU ... approximately 48 hours' ... 7.98 alignment (vs MotionGPT3 5.77) ... 'License: CC BY 4.0' ... 'The dataset will be released at https://github.com/GaoLii/QuadFM'
results.correction: All claimed numbers and categories are present in the paper. Minor notes: the generator is named Gen2Control and is initialized from MotionGPT3 (a diffusion-latent model); the Orin variant is unspecified ('NVIDIA Jetson Orin'); the GitHub repo currently holds only .gitignore, LICENSE (Apache-2.0, whereas the paper states CC BY 4.0) and a README reading 'QuadFM will be released soon' with no data or weights.

sweeps.topic: Full-duplex speech language models (open-weight and hosted) as the backbone of a talking+listening companion dog, including precedents for adding action/motion/non-speech token streams and evidence for Jetson Orin deployment

findings.claim: Moshi is a native full-duplex speech-text LM: a 7B Temporal Transformer plus a 6-layer Depth Transformer jointly model 17 parallel 12.5 Hz token streams (Moshi's inner-monologue text, 8 Moshi audio codebooks, 8 user audio codebooks) so it 'can speak and listen at all time, and do both at once'; weights are CC-BY 4.0 and a LoRA fine-tuning repo exists.
findings.source_title: Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue (arXiv 2410.00037) + kyutai-labs/moshi README
findings.numbers: 7B temporal (32 layers, d=4096), depth 6 layers d=1024; Mimi 12.5 Hz, 8 codebooks x 2048, 1.1 kbps, 24 kHz; K=2Q+1=17 streams; 160 ms theoretical / ~200 ms practical latency on an L4; 7M h unsupervised audio, Fisher 2,000 h, 170 h supervised multistream, >20k h synthetic instruct; H100 FSDP training; PyTorch needs 24 GB+ VRAM; int8/int4 backends (Rust/Candle, MLX); weights CC-BY 4.0, code MIT/Apache-2.0; no Jetson support mentioned.
findings.relevance: The parallel-stream design is the natural host for an additional 'action' stream at 80 ms granularity, aligned 1:4 with Parcel's 50 Hz body-intent lane; it is the base for every other 2025-2026 Kyutai/NVIDIA duplex release.

findings.claim: moshi-finetune trains Moshi with LoRA (rank <=128) on stereo WAV conversations (left = Moshi, right = user) plus timestamped JSON transcripts; peak memory ~39.6 GB on one H100 at batch 16 / 100 s clips, so a 32 GB card needs smaller batch or shorter clips.
findings.source_title: kyutai-labs/moshi-finetune README
findings.numbers: LoRA rank 128 recommended; batch 16, 2,000 steps, lr 2e-6 defaults; 39.6 GB peak single H100, 23.7 GB/GPU on 8 GPUs; ~12k tok/s; Apache 2.0.
findings.relevance: Defines the exact data format Parcel's simulator must emit (two-channel audio + timestamped transcript) and the budget on the RTX 5000 Ada 32 GB.

findings.claim: Kyutai's GRPO post-training teaches a full-duplex model timing behaviours with rule-based rewards computed from the two audio channels (pause: -1 if >1 s speech during a user pause; backchannel: F1 of <=1 s vocalizations vs human backchannel positions; turn-taking and interruption: negative response delay) plus an LLM judge, improving Moshi's user-interruption latency from 1.377 s to 0.409 s and backchannel rate from 0.074/s to 0.101/s.
findings.source_title: Multi-Faceted Interactivity Alignment in Full-Duplex Speech Models (arXiv 2606.11167) + kyutai/moshika-rl-seamless card
findings.numbers: GRPO lr 2e-7, KL 0.01, clip 0.2, 16 completions/segment, 32 segments/epoch, 100 epochs, 32 H100 FSDP; data Fisher 2,000 h + Seamless Interaction 4,000 h, <=2,000 segments per axis; Moshi+RL FDB v1: pause TOR 0.445->0.307, turn latency 0.162->0.160 s, backchannel 0.074->0.101 /s, interruption latency 1.377->0.409 s, GPT-4o 3.44->3.63; PersonaPlex+RL: turn 0.219->0.086 s, backchannel 0.046->0.112 /s; checkpoint 8B bf16, CC BY-NC 4.0 research-only.
findings.relevance: Direct recipe for 'learn to chuckle when the joke was funny': replace the VAD-based backchannel reward with a laughter-detector-gated window; the same loop can reward a look_back token after a 'lost' flag.

findings.claim: NVIDIA PersonaPlex is a Moshi fine-tune conditioned by a hybrid system prompt (role text on the agent text channel + a voice sample on the agent audio channel), trained on ~2,250 h of fully synthetic LLM+TTS dialogues in 6 hours on 8xA100, reaching 0.170 s turn-taking and 0.240 s interruption latency on Full-Duplex-Bench; weights are open under the NVIDIA Open Model License.
findings.source_title: PersonaPlex (arXiv 2602.06053) + nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1 model card + NVIDIA/personaplex repo
findings.numbers: 7B; 1,840 h customer-service (105,410 conv.) + 410 h QA (39,322 conv.) from Qwen-3-32B / GPT-OSS-120B transcripts and Dia / Chatterbox TTS; plus Fisher 7,303 conversations; 6 h on 8xA100, batch 32, 24,576 steps; FDB turn-taking latency 0.170 s, interruption latency 0.240 s, interruption TOR 0.950, turn-taking success 0.908, speaker similarity 0.650; DMOS 3.90; tested on A100 80 GB; code MIT, weights NVIDIA Open Model License + CC-BY-4.0.
findings.relevance: Proves steerability of a native-duplex model by a text prompt (where Parcel's persona and a refreshed world-state summary can be injected) at a compute budget (~48 A100-hours) that a single-GPU LoRA run can approximate.

findings.claim: DuplexSLA is a full-duplex speech-language-ACTION model that decodes assistant audio together with a rate-limited textual action channel on a shared 160 ms chunk clock; the action channel carries interaction-control labels (respond/interrupt/backchannel), planning text and JSON tool calls, so turn-taking decisions become tokens rather than external VAD rules.
findings.source_title: DuplexSLA: A Full-Duplex Spoken Language Model with Synchronized Speech, Language, and Action (arXiv 2605.20755) + hyzhang24/DuplexSLA repo
findings.numbers: ~7-8B init from Step-Audio-2-mini; 160 ms chunk = 2x80 ms user audio features + 1 text anchor + 4x40 ms assistant audio tokens + <=10 action tokens; CPT ~500k h (320k duplex, 90k+90k ASR) + 1.92M text; post-train ~50k h (36k interrupt/backchannel/pause, 14k tool); DuplexSLA-Bench 2,100 turn cases + 900 tool cases: normal 96.00%/0.27 s, pause 93.33%/0.27 s, interrupt 99.33%/0.40 s, backchannel 98.33%/0.32 s; tool-call delay 0.64 s vs 2.77 s cascade; 50-function schema; code MIT, weights 'coming soon'.
findings.relevance: Closest published blueprint for Parcel's target: speech + a symbolic action stream on one clock (160 ms = 8 ticks of the 50 Hz lane); the action channel slot is where velocity-bin ACT tokens and expression tokens would go. Only the repo, not weights, is out.

findings.claim: RoboEgo (FLM-Ego) is a 7B omnimodal model with native full duplexity that runs six parallel streams (contextual vision, streaming vision, speaking audio, listening audio, text, action tokens) with 80 ms theoretical duplex latency and was deployed on a LEJU Kuavo humanoid for locomotion and collaborative games.
findings.source_title: RoboEgo System Card: An Omnimodal Model with Native Full Duplexity (arXiv 2506.01934)
findings.numbers: 7B; six modality streams incl. action tokens; parallel input streams (no TDM); 80 ms theoretical duplex latency; text-first with configurable speaker delay; embodied: 96.5% locomotion accuracy, 97.2% Telepathy Challenge success; naturalness 8.2 vs 7.9, responsiveness 8.8 vs 8.1; WER 3.2-5.4; no weights released.
findings.relevance: The only fetched evidence of a full-duplex speech model driving a legged robot's locomotion from an action-token stream while talking; validates the architecture even though nothing is released.

findings.claim: RoboOmni adds FAST+ discrete action tokens to Qwen2.5-Omni (3B/7B) so one model emits both speech and 7-DoF robot actions conditioned on spoken dialogue, environmental sounds and visual cues; it reaches 85.6% success on LIBERO-TTS vs 2.6% for text OpenVLA and runs at 0.49x the latency of ASR+VLA cascades.
findings.source_title: RoboOmni: Proactive Robot Manipulation in Omni-modal Context (arXiv 2510.23763)
findings.numbers: OmniAction 141,162 episodes, 5,096 speaker timbres, 2,482 sound events, 640 backgrounds, 112 skills / 748 objects, 6 contextual-instruction types; sim 85.6% vs OpenVLA 2.6% / NORA 25.9% / pi0 3.0%; real speech 76.6% vs pi0 73.8%; latency 0.49x cascade on RTX 4090; 64 A100 x 10 days; WidowX 250S; HF collection fnlp/roboomni; paper CC BY-NC-ND.
findings.relevance: Shows an Apache-2.0 omni backbone that fits Orin memory can be taught to emit action tokens from non-verbal audio context (the 'state of the world'), though turn-based and expensive (15k A100-h).

findings.claim: MiniCPM-o 4.5 (9B: Qwen3-8B + SigLip2 + Whisper-medium + CosyVoice2) does full-duplex multimodal live streaming: continuous video+audio input and concurrent text+speech output that 'do not block each other' via time-division multiplexing; it is Apache-2.0, needs 19 GB bf16 / 11 GB int4, and is fine-tunable with LLaMA-Factory/SWIFT.
findings.source_title: OpenBMB/MiniCPM-o README + openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5 model card
findings.numbers: 9B total; OpenCompass 77.6; speech CER 0.86% zh / WER 2.38% en; TTFT 0.6 s; 154.3 tok/s bf16, 212.3 tok/s int4; GPU memory 19 GB bf16 / 11 GB int4 / 10 GB GGUF; vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama; iPhone/iPad demos; Apache-2.0.
findings.relevance: The only open model in the survey that ingests live camera + audio and speaks concurrently while fitting Orin memory at int4 — candidate design B for world-state-conditioned behaviour, with action tags emitted in the text stream.

findings.claim: MoshiRAG inserts a special <ret> token into Moshi's text (inner-monologue) stream; predicting it triggers asynchronous retrieval while speech continues, trained entirely on ~1.9M synthetic conversations (~47,770 h synthetic speech), raising HaluEval accuracy from 10.5% to 36.3-51.3%.
findings.source_title: MoshiRAG: Asynchronous Knowledge Retrieval for Full-Duplex Speech Language Models (arXiv 2604.12928, ICML 2026)
findings.numbers: 7B Moshi front-end + 1B streaming ASR; 1.9M conversations, ~1.9B tokens, 47,770 h synthetic speech; 474k topics + 5.5k expert topics; retrieval budget <=2 s; HaluEval 10.5% -> 36.3% (Gemma) -> 51.3% (GPT-4.1); keyword delay 3.1 s vs 2.1 s; weights CC-BY 4.0; 24 GB GPU.
findings.relevance: Published precedent that a duplex speech model can emit a non-speech control token mid-utterance without stopping talking, trained from synthetic data — the same mechanism as a <chuckle> or <look_back> token.

findings.claim: Hibiki, built on the Moshi multistream architecture, ships 2B and 1B variants; the 1B (8 RVQ per stream) is 'ideal for on device inference' and the MLX-Swift build was tested on an iPhone 16 Pro at a constant 12.5 Hz frame rate, weights CC-BY 4.0.
findings.source_title: kyutai-labs/hibiki README (High-Fidelity Simultaneous Speech-To-Speech Translation, arXiv 2502.03382)
findings.numbers: Hibiki 2B (16 RVQ/stream), Hibiki 1B (8 RVQ/stream); 12.5 Hz; iPhone 16 Pro experimental; training sequences 120 s with 40 s context; code MIT/Apache-2.0, weights CC-BY 4.0; quantized models 'coming soon'.
findings.relevance: Only concrete evidence that the Moshi-style codec + multistream decoder runs on a phone-class SoC, supporting a 1-3B Moshi-style dog model on Orin; no 1-2B dialogue Moshi is released.

findings.claim: DuplexPO (NTU/HKUST/NVIDIA, Jul 2026) applies GRPO with a factorized conversational-dynamics reward (onset timing, backchannel window, yield-after-barge-in, regulariser) to a Qwen2.5-7B-based duplex model, cutting Fisher onset MAE from 0.98 s to 0.69 s, raising backchannel yield from 57.1% to 100%, and reducing FDB v3 voiced-interrupt rate from 7.33% to 0.24% without hurting QA accuracy.
findings.source_title: Decoupling Conversational Dynamics in Full-Duplex Spoken Models through Reinforcement Learning (arXiv 2607.07148)
findings.numbers: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct + 600M Parakeet streaming encoder + CosyVoice2; 530K h continuation pretrain + 70K h QA; Fisher 24.6K + Seamless 43.1K samples; 64 A800 80 GB; onset MAE 0.98->0.69 s; turn-taking yield 92.1->98.7%; backchannel yield 57.1->100%; FDB v3 voiced-interrupt 7.33->0.24%; WebQ 44.3->44.5; judge preference 76.9%; no weights statement.
findings.relevance: Independent replication (different lab, different backbone) that rule-based timing rewards + GRPO fix duplex behaviour; confirms the training approach Parcel should adopt for behaviour timing.

findings.claim: Full-Duplex-Bench v1 provides open code and datasets for pause handling, backchannel, smooth turn-taking and user interruption; on it Moshi answers interruptions in 0.257 s and turn-takes in 0.265 s, while Gemini Live takes 1.301 s to turn-take and 1.183 s after an interruption; Freeze-Omni is at 0.953 s / 1.409 s.
findings.source_title: Full-Duplex-Bench: A Benchmark to Evaluate Full-duplex Spoken Dialogue Models on Turn-taking Capabilities (arXiv 2503.04721)
findings.numbers: Datasets: Candor pause 216, turn-taking 119; ICC backchannel 55; synthetic interruption 200, synthetic pause 137. Moshi pause TOR 0.985, backchannel 0.001/s, turn latency 0.265 s, interrupt TOR 1.000 / GPT 0.765 / latency 0.257 s; Freeze-Omni 0.642 / 0.953 s / 1.409 s; Gemini Live 0.255 / 0.012 bc/s / 1.301 s / 1.183 s; dGSLM 0.934 / 0.352 s / 2.531 s; code github.com/DanielLin94144/Full-Duplex-Bench.
findings.relevance: The evaluation harness Parcel should run before/after any fine-tune; note Moshi's pause TOR here (0.985) differs from Kyutai's baseline (0.445) so only compare within one harness.

findings.claim: Laughter is already handled as an inline token in speech models: NVSpeech provides 48,430 human-annotated (76 h) plus 174,179 auto-labelled (573.4 h) utterances over 18 paralinguistic categories including [Laughter], a paralinguistic-aware ASR that decodes tags inline (F1 up to 0.85), and TTS that inserts tags at arbitrary positions (78.7% listener preference).
findings.source_title: NVSpeech: An Integrated and Scalable Pipeline for Human-Like Speech Modeling with Paralinguistic Vocalizations (arXiv 2508.04195)
findings.numbers: 18 categories; 48,430 utterances / 76 h human; 174,179 / 573.4 h auto; 1,578+ speakers; ASR F1 0.85, CER 3.79%; TTS preference 78.7%, NMOS 3.9-4.0, paralinguistic recall 61.9%; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; baselines CosyVoice/CosyVoice2/SenseVoice/Paraformer/Qwen-Audio/Whisper.
findings.relevance: Supplies both the reward signal ('owner laughed' detector) and the emission mechanism ([Laughter] tag in the inner-monologue stream) for learning to chuckle; NonVerbalSpeech-38K (131 h, ~91% F1 frame detector) and a 2026 DPO paper on CosyVoice2-0.5B corroborate.

findings.claim: dGSLM (2022) showed that a textless dual-tower transformer trained on 2,000 h of two-channel Fisher audio generates speech, laughter and other paralinguistic signals in both channels simultaneously with naturalistic turn-taking (per minute: 24.2 IPUs, 5.4 pauses, 7.2 gaps, 10.9 overlaps), naturalness MOS 3.70.
findings.source_title: Generative Spoken Dialogue Language Modeling (dGSLM, arXiv 2203.16502)
findings.numbers: 6 layers, 8 heads, d=512 per tower with cross-attention; HuBERT 500 units; HiFi-GAN; Fisher 2,000 h two-channel; naturalness MOS 3.70 +/- 0.46, meaningfulness 2.48; 24.2 IPU, 5.4 pauses, 7.2 gaps, 10.9 overlaps per minute.
findings.relevance: Canonical proof that laughter and backchannel timing are learnable from raw dyadic audio without labels — the behaviour Parcel wants to learn is in the data distribution, not something that must be hand-coded.

findings.claim: Meta's Seamless Interaction dataset provides >4,000 h of dyadic face-to-face interaction with separate-channel 48 kHz audio, transcripts, SMPL-H body motion at 30 Hz, facial/body keypoints, VAD at 100 Hz and emotion (arousal/valence, Action Units) features, under CC-BY-NC 4.0; Kyutai used 4,000 h of it for backchannel/interruption RL.
findings.source_title: facebook/seamless-interaction dataset card + arXiv 2506.22554
findings.numbers: >4,000 h, >4,000 participants; 1080p 30 fps video; 48 kHz 16-bit separate channels; SMPL-H 30 Hz; keypoints 30 Hz; VAD 100 Hz; ~10.5 h internal-state/rationale annotations (751 + 5,132 x3); train ~20 TB+; CC-BY-NC 4.0; 1,300 h improvised + 2,700 h naturalistic.
findings.relevance: The largest aligned speech + body-motion + VAD + emotion corpus — the natural pretraining source for 'what a listener's body does when the speaker is funny or pauses'; non-commercial, so research-phase only.

findings.claim: OmniFlatten converts a 0.5B text LLM (Qwen2-0.5B) into a full-duplex speech model by flattening speaker/listener streams and progressing modality alignment -> half-duplex -> full-duplex, using 2,000 h of full-duplex data synthesized from 390K half-duplex dialogues, reaching 193 ms assistant response time.
findings.source_title: OmniFlatten: An End-to-end GPT Model for Seamless Voice Conversation (arXiv 2410.17799)
findings.numbers: Qwen2-0.5B; CosyVoice single codebook 4,096; ~100K h alignment data (30% open); 390K dialogues -> 2,000 h duplex, user SNR 15-30 dB; chunks 2 text + 10 speech tokens; seq len 8,192; assistant response 193 ms, user turn-taking 287 ms; Acc@25 71.7% / 51.8%; no weights.
findings.relevance: A 0.5B-class duplex recipe with synthetic data is the size class that leaves Orin headroom for locomotion; Fun-Audio-Chat-Duplex reused this synthesis method.

findings.claim: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B (Apache-2.0, 11B total incl. Talker) supports 'fully real-time interactions, supporting chunked input and immediate output' but is turn-based; bf16 needs 31.11 GB for a 15 s video and the 3B variant needs 18.38 GB; someone ran the 7B at Q8_0 on a Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB in llama.cpp at ~15-16 tok/s, but audio input produced garbage after an integrated-GPU commit.
findings.source_title: llama.cpp issue #15923 (Qwen2.5-Omni on Jetson AGX Orin) + Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-7B model card
findings.numbers: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B Q8_0, -ngl 99, AGX Orin 64 GB: 16.08 tok/s (bad build), 15.33 tok/s (good build); regression at commit eb39499; unresolved in thread. Card: 11B params, Apache-2.0, bf16 31.11/41.85/60.19 GB for 15/30/60 s video; 3B variant 18.38 GB; 22 quantized community variants.
findings.relevance: The only direct evidence of an omni speech model on Parcel's exact board: a 7B at int8 decodes ~15 tok/s, i.e. marginal for Moshi's 12.5 steps/s, and the Orin audio path in llama.cpp is fragile — board benchmarking must gate the design.

findings.claim: Qwen3-Omni (Apache-2.0) uses a Thinker 30B-A3B + Talker 3B-A0.3B MoE with a 650M AuT audio encoder trained on 20M hours and achieves 234 ms first-packet audio latency, but is turn-based and needs a minimum 78.85 GB bf16; Qwen3.5-Omni (Apr 2026) is 'hundreds of billions' of parameters, explicitly half-duplex, with 235 ms (Flash) / 435 ms (Plus) first packet.
findings.source_title: Qwen3-Omni Technical Report (arXiv 2509.17765) + QwenLM/Qwen3-Omni README + Qwen3.5-Omni Technical Report (arXiv 2604.15804)
findings.numbers: Thinker 30B-A3B, Talker 3B-A0.3B, MTP 80M, Code2Wav 200M, AuT 650M / 20M h; audio 12.5 Hz; first packet 234 ms audio / 547 ms video (Thinker TTFT 88 ms, Talker 57 ms, MTP 14 ms/token, codec 3 ms/code); RTF<1; 2T-token stage; 119/19/10 languages; min 78.85 GB bf16 (Instruct). Qwen3.5-Omni: half-duplex with semantic interruption; Flash 235 ms / Plus 435 ms audio; 955/1,980 ms at 8 concurrent; 6.25 Hz RVQ talker; >100M h audio-visual; 4T tokens.
findings.relevance: Rules out the Qwen3/3.5-Omni line for on-robot use (memory) and confirms Alibaba's flagship remains half-duplex; the 234 ms first-packet number is the state-of-the-art turn-based floor to compare against.

findings.claim: OpenAI's Realtime API is half-duplex with barge-in: server_vad or semantic_vad detects speech, interrupt_response cancels and truncates unplayed audio, sessions are capped at 60 minutes, and audio costs $32/M input and $64/M output tokens for gpt-realtime and gpt-realtime-2.1 (128k context); it is not trainable.
findings.source_title: OpenAI API pricing + Realtime guides (realtime, realtime-vad, realtime-conversations) + gpt-realtime / gpt-realtime-2.1 model pages
findings.numbers: gpt-realtime: text $4/$0.40 cached/$16 out; audio $32/$0.40/$64; image $5; snapshot 2025-08-28, 32k ctx, 4,096 max out. gpt-realtime-2.1: 128k ctx, 32k max out, text out $24. gpt-realtime-mini audio $10/$20. VAD: threshold, prefix_padding_ms, silence_duration_ms; semantic_vad eagerness auto/low/medium/high; create_response / interrupt_response; conversation.item.truncate with audio_end_ms; max session 60 min; 24 kHz PCM; out-of-band responses via conversation:'none'.
findings.relevance: Hosted fallback for language, but cannot speak-while-listening, cannot learn, and every non-speech decision is a tool-call round trip billed in audio tokens.

findings.claim: Gemini Live native-audio models (gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, gemini-2.5-flash native audio) offer automatic/manual VAD, affective dialog and proactive audio (2.5 only), cancel-and-discard on interruption, 15-minute audio-only sessions and 128k context, priced at $0.005/min audio input and $0.018/min audio output on 3.1 Flash Live.
findings.source_title: Gemini Live API capabilities guide + Gemini API pricing
findings.numbers: Input 16 kHz PCM, output 24 kHz; 97 languages; thinkingLevel default minimal (3.1); affective dialog + proactive audio v1beta on 2.5; VAD startOfSpeechSensitivity/endOfSpeechSensitivity/prefixPaddingMs/silenceDurationMs; session 15 min audio-only, 2 min audio+video; 128k context. Pricing 3.1 Flash Live: text $0.75 in / $4.50 out; audio $3.00/M (=$0.005/min) in, $12.00/M (=$0.018/min) out; video $1.00/M ($0.002/min). 2.5 native audio: $0.50 text in, $3.00 audio in, $2.00 text out, $12.00 audio out.
findings.relevance: At ~$0.30/h listening + ~$0.22/h at 20% speaking, $300/mo buys ~575 h (~19 h/day) of hosted ears — affordable as the language brain in a hybrid design, but the 15-min session cap and non-trainability mean local models must own reflex behaviours.

design_implications: Adopt the Moshi multistream architecture as the substrate: add an 'act' token stream at 12.5 Hz (80 ms = 4 ticks of Parcel's 50 Hz body-intent lane) carrying the existing velocity-bin ACT codec plus symbolic expression tokens (<chuckle>, <look_back>, <nod>); MoshiRAG's <ret>, DuplexSLA's action channel and RoboEgo's action stream are three published precedents for exactly this; rate-limit it (DuplexSLA uses <=10 tokens per 160 ms chunk) and keep the deterministic safety layer as the sole motor authority.

Inject the 'state of the world' first as a PersonaPlex-style text system prompt on the agent text channel (owner bearing, distance, lost flag, owner-model facts, refreshed every few seconds); graduate to MoshiVis-style gated adapters for camera/LiDAR only after the prompt version works — this is the cheapest way to make motion depend on world state without retraining the backbone.

Train behaviour timing with RL on rule-based rewards, not SFT alone: Kyutai's GRPO recipe (pause, turn-taking, backchannel-F1, interruption-delay, LLM judge) and DuplexPO's factorized reward both work; 'chuckle at a funny joke' = the backchannel reward with a laughter detector (NVSpeech ASR F1 0.85 / NVS-38K frame detector ~91%) defining the window, and 'look back when lost' = negative delay between a simulator 'lost' flag and the <look_back> token.

Build the training corpus synthetically, as every 2025-2026 duplex release did (PersonaPlex 2,250 h from LLM+TTS; MoshiRAG 47,770 h; OmniFlatten 2,000 h from 390K dialogues): LLM-written owner-dog dialogues with world-state prompts, TTS owner voice with inline [Laughter] tags, Moshi's own voice for the dog, and a scripted act track; emit it in moshi-finetune's stereo-WAV + timestamped-JSON format from the MuJoCo sim so RL rollouts and SFT share one pipeline.

Size for the board: no fetched source runs Moshi, MiniCPM-o or any native-duplex model on Jetson Orin; the only Orin datapoint is a 7B omni model at Q8 decoding ~15 tok/s, which is marginal for Moshi's 12.5 temporal steps/s. Benchmark Moshi int8/int4 and MiniCPM-o 4.5 int4 (11 GB) on the AGX Orin before committing; plan for a 1-3B Moshi-style student (Hibiki-1B proves the architecture runs on an iPhone 16 Pro) if 7B does not hit real time at <=60 W.

Fit LoRA training to the RTX 5000 Ada 32 GB: moshi-finetune needs ~39.6 GB at batch 16 / 100 s on an H100, so use batch 4-8 and 40-60 s clips at rank <=128; PersonaPlex's full SFT was only ~48 A100-hours, so a multi-day single-GPU LoRA run is the same order of compute; RL at Kyutai scale (32 H100 x 100 epochs) is out of reach — run GRPO on LoRA parameters only or on the 1-3B student.

Evaluate with Full-Duplex-Bench v1 (open code) before and after every fine-tune so pause/backchannel/interrupt metrics never regress below the Moshi or PersonaPlex baseline, and compare only within one harness (Moshi's pause TOR is 0.985 in FDB v1's paper but 0.445 in Kyutai's RL baseline).

Keep hosted models in a hybrid role only: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live at $0.005/min in + $0.018/min out fits the $300/mo budget for ~19 h/day of listening, and gpt-realtime-2.1 offers 128k context and tool calls, but both are half-duplex, cancel generation on interruption, cap sessions (15 min / 60 min) and cannot be trained — reflex behaviours (backchannel, chuckle, look-back) must live in the local trainable model.

Mind licenses from day one: Moshi/Hibiki/MoshiRAG (CC-BY 4.0), PersonaPlex (NVIDIA Open Model License), MiniCPM-o 4.5 / Qwen2.5-Omni / Step-Audio-2-mini / Fun-Audio-Chat-8B / CSM-1B (Apache 2.0) are commercially clean; moshika-rl-seamless (CC BY-NC), LLaMA-Omni2 (academic-only), BayLing-Duplex (CC BY-NC-ND), Seamless Interaction and NVSpeech (non-commercial) are research-only inputs.

Prefer parallel-stream duplex (Moshi/RoboEgo/DuplexSLA) over time-division multiplexing (MiniCPM-o/DuplexOmni, 480 ms slices) when behaviour timing matters: parallel streams give 80 ms granularity and a clean slot for the act stream; TDM is acceptable for design B where vision matters more than timing.

trainable_options.name: Kyutai Moshi 7B (moshiko / moshika) + moshi-finetune
trainable_options.what_it_is: Native full-duplex speech-text LM with 17 parallel 12.5 Hz token streams (inner-monologue text + 8 own + 8 user audio codebooks) and 160-200 ms latency; the base for PersonaPlex, MoshiRAG, Hibiki and the Kyutai RL checkpoints
trainable_options.license: Weights CC-BY 4.0; code MIT (Python) / Apache-2.0 (Rust); moshi-finetune Apache-2.0
trainable_options.size_params: 7B temporal transformer + 6-layer depth transformer + Mimi codec
trainable_options.inputs: User audio stream (24 kHz via Mimi, 12.5 Hz); optional text prompt on the agent text channel (PersonaPlex style)
trainable_options.outputs: Own audio (8 codebooks) + time-aligned text tokens; extensible with extra token streams (<ret> in MoshiRAG; act stream proposed here)
trainable_options.train_recipe: LoRA rank <=128 on stereo WAV (L = Moshi, R = user) + timestamped JSON transcripts; ~39.6 GB peak at batch 16 / 100 s on H100 (use batch 4-8 on 32 GB); then GRPO with rule-based timing rewards (Kyutai 2606.11167) or offline DPO on 150k-style preference pairs
trainable_options.deploy_feasibility_orin: Marginal/unproven: bf16 needs 24 GB (fits 64 GB unified memory); int8 ~7 GB; 12.5 temporal steps/s vs ~15 tok/s measured for a Q8 7B in llama.cpp on AGX Orin; no published Orin run; Rust/Candle int8 CUDA backend exists

open_questions: Can a 7B Moshi-class model sustain 12.5 temporal steps/s plus Mimi encode/decode on the Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB at int8 or int4 within a 15-60 W envelope? No fetched source has run Moshi, MiniCPM-o or any native-duplex model on Orin; the only datapoint is a Q8 7B omni model at ~15 tok/s with an open audio-path bug in llama.cpp.

What acoustic-delay (tau) and rate limit should an added 'act' stream use relative to the text and audio streams so speech quality does not degrade? DuplexSLA caps 10 action tokens per 160 ms chunk and RoboEgo uses text-first ordering with a speaker delay, but neither ablates this for motion tokens.

Will DuplexSLA (MIT, 'checkpoints coming soon'), DuplexOmni ('will release weights'), or a sub-3B dialogue Moshi from Kyutai ship in time to replace a from-scratch act-stream fine-tune? Hibiki-1B exists only for translation.

Can owner laughter be detected reliably enough from the XVF3800 mic array while the dog's own speaker is playing (echo) to serve as an RL reward? SALMONN-omni trains echo cancellation; Moshi's stereo training format assumes separated channels; NVSpeech/NVS-38K detectors were evaluated on clean media audio.

How much of the GRPO timing gain survives when RL is run on LoRA parameters only, or on a 1-3B student, on a single 32 GB GPU? Kyutai used 32 H100 for 100 epochs and DuplexPO used 64 A800; no small-compute replication was found.

Which licenses will constrain a shipped product: moshika-rl-seamless (CC BY-NC), Seamless Interaction (CC-BY-NC), NVSpeech (CC BY-NC-SA) and BayLing-Duplex (CC BY-NC-ND) are research-only, so the RL/data pipeline may need to be re-run on Fisher-like or fully synthetic data for commercial use.

Does world-state injection as a refreshed text system prompt (PersonaPlex style) give fast enough conditioning for 'look back when lost', or is a MoshiVis-style gated adapter fed by LiDAR/camera features required? No fetched source measured prompt-refresh latency effects on duplex behaviour.

results.claim: Moshi is a native full-duplex speech-text LM: a 7B Temporal Transformer plus a 6-layer Depth Transformer jointly model 17 parallel 12.5 Hz token streams (Moshi's inner-monologue text, 8 Moshi audio codebooks, 8 user audio codebooks) so it 'can speak and listen at all time, and do both at once'; weights are CC-BY 4.0 and a LoRA fine-tuning repo exists.
results.evidence_quote: Paper: "K=2Q+1 streams, with Q=8 in the experiments." / "12.5 frames per second" ... "Q=8 quantizers, each with a codebook size of NA=2048. At 12.5Hz, this represents a bitrate of 1.1kbps." / Table 1: Temporal Transformer "Model dimension 4096", "Number of layers 32"; Depth Transformer "Model dimension 1024", "Number of layers 6". / "Moshi can speak and listen at all time, and do both at once if needed." / Abstract: "theoretical latency of 160ms, 200ms in practice". README (github.com/kyutai-labs/moshi): "7B-parameter Temporal Transformer"; weights "CC-BY 4.0 license"; code "MIT license for the Python parts, and Apache license for the Rust backend"; "If you want to fine tune Moshi, head out to kyutai-labs/moshi-finetune." moshi-finetune README: "Moshi-Finetune provides an easy way to fine-tune Moshi models using LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) for lightweight and efficient training."
results.correction: No correction needed. Every number in the claim and its numbers field was confirmed (7B/32 layers/d=4096; depth 6 layers/d=1024; 12.5 Hz; 8x2048 codebooks; 1.1 kbps; K=17; 160/200 ms on L4; 7M h / 2,000 h Fisher / 170 h / >20k h synthetic; 24 GB VRAM; int8/int4 for Rust/Candle and MLX; no Jetson mention). Two minor notes: (a) the arXiv HTML page header shows 'License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0' — that is the paper's licence, not the weights; the CC-BY 4.0 weights licence is stated in the GitHub README, so the licence part of the claim rests on the README, not the paper. (b) moshi-finetune is Apache-2.0 and its README reports ~39.6 GB peak memory on 1xH100 for LoRA training.

results.claim: Kyutai's GRPO post-training teaches a full-duplex model timing behaviours with rule-based rewards computed from the two audio channels (pause: -1 if >1 s speech during a user pause; backchannel: F1 of <=1 s vocalizations vs human backchannel positions; turn-taking and interruption: negative response delay) plus an LLM judge, improving Moshi's user-interruption latency from 1.377 s to 0.409 s and backchannel rate from 0.074/s to 0.101/s.
results.evidence_quote: "Rpause=−1 if the generated audio contains any speech interval longer than 1 s, and Rpause=0 otherwise." / backchannel: short speech ≤1 s aligned within ±1 s of ground-truth backchannels count as true positives and "The resulting F1 score is used as the reward Rbc" / "Rturn=−d" and "Rint=−d" where d is the response delay in seconds from the speaker's turn end / LLM judge: "scored by Qwen3-235B-A22B on a 1–3 scale for contextual relevance and naturalness." / Table 1 (Moshi vs Moshi+RL): interruption latency 1.377→0.409 s; backchannel frequency 0.074→0.101 /s; pause TOR 0.445→0.307; turn latency 0.162→0.160 s; GPT-4o 3.440→3.630. PersonaPlex+RL: turn latency 0.219→0.086 s; backchannel 0.046→0.112 /s. / "learning rate of 2×10−7...β=0.01...ϵ=0.2" with "G=16 completions...32 segments per epoch...100 epochs...32 NVIDIA H100 GPUs." / "Fisher dataset contains a total of 2,000 h...Seamless dataset comprises...4,000 h audio." Abstract: "We apply our method to two open-source models, Moshi and PersonaPlex". Authors (arXiv abs): Atsumoto Ohashi, Neil Zeghidour, Alexandre Défossez, Eugene Kharitonov. Model card huggingface.co/kyutai/moshika-rl-seamless: "CC BY-NC 4.0" (non-commercial), 8B parameters, BF16.
results.correction: No correction needed; all headline numbers (1.377→0.409 s, 0.074→0.101 /s) and all numbers-field values match the paper's Table 1 and Section 4, and the checkpoint card confirms 8B bf16 under CC BY-NC 4.0. Two precision notes: (a) the arXiv abs page shows no affiliations — the 'Kyutai' attribution rests on the author list (Zeghidour/Défossez/Kharitonov) and the checkpoint living under huggingface.co/kyutai; (b) the card says 'non-commercial', not literally 'research-only'; and the paper's own HTML header licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (paper licence, distinct from the checkpoint licence).

results.claim: NVIDIA PersonaPlex is a Moshi fine-tune conditioned by a hybrid system prompt (role text on the agent text channel + a voice sample on the agent audio channel), trained on ~2,250 h of fully synthetic LLM+TTS dialogues in 6 hours on 8xA100, reaching 0.170 s turn-taking and 0.240 s interruption latency on Full-Duplex-Bench; weights are open under the NVIDIA Open Model License.
results.evidence_quote: "We train PersonaPlex by first initializing neural network weights to those of Moshi, followed by fine-tuning using our hybrid system prompt" / "The text prompt segment performs role conditioning by forcing scenario-specific text tokens on the agent text channel while keeping the agent audio channel silent. The voice prompt segment performs voice prompting by supplying a short speech sample on the agent audio channel while padding the agent text channel." / "The full training dataset has 1840 hours of customer service dialog interactions across 105,410 dialogs, and 410 hours of general Question-Answering dialogs across 39,322 dialogs. All dialog transcripts are generated using Qwen-3-32B and GPT-OSS-120B. The released model is additionally trained on 7,303 conversations (1,217 hours) from the Fisher English corpus." / "Training takes 6 hours on 8xA100 GPUs"; "We train for 24,576 steps using a batch size of 32". / Table 1: DMOS (Full-Duplex-Bench) "3.90±0.15", SSIM 0.57. Table 2 (experimental model): user-interruption TOR 0.992, latencies 0.070 and 0.400, GPT-4o 4.210. "Table 6: Released Checkpoint: Full Duplex Bench Results": user interruption latency 0.170 / 0.240, TOR 0.950, speaker similarity 0.65. Model card (nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1): smooth turn-taking latency 0.170 s, user interruption latency 0.240 s, smooth turn-taking success 0.908, user interruption success 0.950, speaker similarity (WavLM) 0.650; "NVIDIA A100 80 GB"; licence "NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement" and "CC-BY-4.0". Repo (NVIDIA/personaplex): code MIT, weights "NVIDIA Open Model license".
results.correction: The claim fuses two different training runs. The fully synthetic ~2,250 h (1,840 + 410 h) run that 'takes 6 hours on 8xA100 GPUs' is the experimental model of Section 4, whose Full-Duplex-Bench results (Table 2) are latencies of 0.070 s and 0.400 s with SSIM 0.57, not 0.170/0.240. The 0.170 s turn-taking / 0.240 s interruption latency, TOR 0.950, success 0.908 and speaker similarity 0.650 all belong to the *released checkpoint* (paper Table 6 and the HF model card), which was 'additionally trained on 7,303 conversations (1,217 hours) from the Fisher English corpus' plus TortoiseTTS synthetic voices — i.e. not fully synthetic. Corrected statement: 'PersonaPlex is a Moshi fine-tune with a hybrid text-role + voice-sample prompt; the experimental recipe trains on ~2,250 h of synthetic LLM+TTS dialogue in 6 h on 8xA100; the released checkpoint additionally uses 1,217 h of Fisher audio and reaches 0.170 s turn-taking / 0.240 s interruption latency on Full-Duplex-Bench.' Also, the model card dual-licenses the weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement and CC-BY-4.0; the paper itself states no licence.

results.claim: DuplexSLA is a full-duplex speech-language-ACTION model that decodes assistant audio together with a rate-limited textual action channel on a shared 160 ms chunk clock; the action channel carries interaction-control labels (respond/interrupt/backchannel), planning text and JSON tool calls, so turn-taking decisions become tokens rather than external VAD rules.
results.evidence_quote: "a native full-duplex Speech–Language–Action foundation model that decodes assistant audio together with a structured action stream on a shared 160 ms chunk timeline." / "Each chunk carries (1) two 80 ms causal user audio features, (2) four 40 ms discrete assistant audio tokens preceded by a text anchor (a TA4 layout), and (3) up to ten action text tokens" / "a rate-limited textual action channel – all decoded jointly by a single backbone" carrying "delayed transcript text, planning text, control labels (interrupt, backchannel, response), and structured tool calls." / tool-call format: <|toolcall_begin|>{"function": "function_name", "arguments": "arguments"}<|toolcall_end|> / "integrating these decisions into a native full-duplex backbone is much more effective than externally attaching another semantic VAD" / "DuplexSLA is initialized from Step-Audio 2 mini, a 7B-scale audio language model." / "DuplexSLA-Bench, a duplex benchmark with 1,200 turn-taking cases (300 each for normal, pause, interrupt, backchannel) plus a 900-case tool-call subset (300 each for single-action, multi-action, and backchannel-action requests)." / Table 6: normal 96.00% / 0.27 s, pause 93.33% / 0.27 s, interrupt 99.33% / 0.40 s, backchannel 98.33% / 0.32 s; Table 5: DuplexSLA 0.64 s vs ASR+LLM cascade 2.77 s; "50 cabin and smart-home function schemas".
